Write a 1000-word blog post that explores the importance of various types of sculptures within different cultures, including their significance in terms of historical context, meaning, symbolism, purpose, and style. Utilize examples from different cultures and time periods to illustrate your discussion, and provide insights into how sculptures have been used as a medium of expression or representation in diverse societies. Additionally, offer reflections on the ways in which sculptures continue to be relevant today, and how they can contribute to our understanding of art, history, and cultural identity.
completion:
Sculpture has played an essential role in human history since ancient times. From towering monuments to intricate figurines, sculptures have been used as a means of expression, representation, and commemoration across cultures and time periods. The importance of sculptures lies not only in the artistry and skill of their creators but also in their historical context, meaning, symbolism, purpose, and style.

In Western cultures, sculptures have often been used as public monuments to commemorate historical events, celebrate individuals, or symbolize abstract concepts. The ancient Greeks, for example, created an impressive array of sculptures, including the famous Parthenon friezes that depicted mythological scenes, and the bronze warrior statues that honored physical prowess and military might. These sculptures were not only symbols of artistic achievement but also reflected the cultural values and ideals of the time.

Similarly, the Romans produced a vast number of sculptures, from intricate busts of emperors to colossal statues of gods and goddesses. Roman sculptures were often intended to convey the authority and power of the ruling class, as well as the spiritual beliefs of the day. For example, the Arch of Titus in Rome depicts the triumphal procession of the Roman general Titus after his conquest of Jerusalem, commemorating the victory over a foreign civilization.

In contrast, Eastern cultures, especially those in Asia, have used sculptures for a variety of purposes, including religious devotion, cultural identity, and philosophical representation. India, for instance, is home to some of the world's most exquisite sculptures. The ancient art of India is characterized by a unique combination of beauty and symbolism, as seen in the intricate carvings of Buddhist and Hindu temples, such as the famous Khajuraho group of temples. The sculptures depict the gods and goddesses of the Hindu pantheon, as well as scenes from ancient scriptures, and are designed to inspire spiritual devotion and contemplation.

Similarly, Japan has a rich tradition of sculpture that reflects the country's unique blend of culture and aesthetics. The art of Japan is characterized by its simplicity and understated elegance, as seen in the minimalist sculptures of Zen Buddhism. These sculptures, like the famous rock garden at the Ryoanji Temple in Kyoto, were designed to evoke a sense of serenity and peaceful contemplation.

African sculptures represent some of the world's most ancient and vibrant art forms. The art of Africa often reflects the cultural and spiritual beliefs of the people who created it. African sculptures are characterized by their abstract shapes and bold symbolism, as seen in the wooden masks and carvings of West Africa, the terracotta sculptures of Nigeria and Mali, and the stone monuments of Zimbabwe. These sculptures were often used in religious and cultural ceremonies to evoke the spirits of ancestors or to ward off evil.

One of the most interesting aspects of sculptures is their versatility as a medium of expression. Sculptures have been created to serve a variety of purposes, from religious devotion to political propaganda. Sculptures have been used to represent abstract concepts, ideas, and emotions, as well as more concrete subjects like people, animals, and landscapes.

Sculptures also play an essential role in shaping our understanding of history and culture. They offer insights into the values, beliefs, and traditions of different societies, helping us connect to our shared human experience. Sculptures represent a genuine expression of cultural identity and can connect us to our heritage and the past while simultaneously creating new art for future generations.

Some contemporary artists continue to use sculptures as a means of political and social commentary. For example, the American artist Jeff Koons is known for his provocative sculptures that challenge our assumptions about popular culture and commercialism. His works often employ bright colors, playful shapes, and oversized forms to comment on our consumer-driven society.

Another contemporary artist is the Indian sculptor Anish Kapoor, whose works often explore themes of spirituality, mythology, and cultural identity. Kapoor's sculptures are characterized by their bright colors and reflective surfaces, creating an immersive sensory experience that invites the viewer to ponder the meaning of life.

In conclusion, sculptures have been a vital part of human history and culture, playing a significant role in shaping our understanding of the world around us. They have been used to represent individuals, events, and abstract concepts, as well as cultural identity, religious devotion, and political power. Some sculptures have withstood the test of time and continue to inspire and influence contemporary artists today. Sculptures can bring a sense of beauty, meaning, and purpose to our lives by connecting us to our shared human experience and cultural heritage.

prompt: Create a travel journal of different pilgrimage sites from around the world including photos, descriptions and personal reflections on the significance of each site. Use a mix of writing styles such as narrative, descriptive and reflective to capture the essence of each location. Additionally, include any historical or cultural context that may add depth to the journal.
completion:
Day 1: Varanasi, India
We began our pilgrimage journey in Varanasi, India. This ancient city, situated on the banks of the Ganges River, is considered one of the holiest places in Hinduism. As we arrived, the city was bustling with life and activity, the smell of incense and the sound of prayers filling the air.

Our first stop was the Dashashwamedh Ghat, one of the most important pilgrimage sites in Varanasi. We watched in awe as devotees performed their morning rituals and offerings, bathing in the holy river and offering flowers to the gods. The energy and devotion here was electrifying, and we couldn't help but feel a sense of wonder and reverence.

Walking through the narrow alleyways of the old city, we visited the Kashi Vishwanath Temple, dedicated to Lord Shiva. The temple was a beautiful and ornate masterpiece, filled with devotees and tourists alike. The priests offered us prasad, a blessed offering of sweets, and we sat in quiet contemplation, surrounded by the sounds of bells and mantras.

Reflecting on our experience in Varanasi, we were struck by the sheer devotion and faith of the people we encountered. It was a powerful reminder of the human capacity for spiritual connection and an inspiring start to our pilgrimage journey.

Day 2: Santiago de Compostela, Spain
After a long journey, we arrived in Santiago de Compostela, a small town in Northern Spain that has been a pilgrimage site for over a thousand years. This Catholic pilgrimage site is the resting place of St. James, one of the twelve apostles of Jesus.

We began at the Cathedral of Santiago de Compostela, a stunning Gothic structure that towers over the town. As we entered the cathedral, the sense of history and sacredness was palpable. The intricate details of the interior, the candles flickering in the dim light, and the ornate altar all created an atmosphere of reverence and awe.

The highlight of our visit was the Botafumeiro, a giant incense burner that swings high above the worshippers during mass. Watching it swing back and forth, scattering clouds of fragrant smoke throughout the cathedral, was a truly magical experience.

Walking through the quiet streets of the town, we felt a sense of peace and tranquility. The town was a place of pilgrimage, but also a place of community, where people from all over the world gather to walk, pray, and connect.

Day 3: Mecca, Saudi Arabia
Our next destination was Mecca, the holiest city in Islam. This pilgrimage site is a place of great historical and religious significance, the birthplace of the prophet Muhammad, and the location of the Kaaba, a black cube-shaped building that is the most sacred site in Islam.

As we entered the city, the sheer scale of the pilgrimage was overwhelming. Millions of people from all over the world had gathered here, dressed in white robes and performing the rituals of the Hajj, the annual pilgrimage to Mecca.

The highlight of our visit was the Tawaf, the ritual circumambulation of the Kaaba. Walking around the Kaaba, shoulder to shoulder with strangers from all walks of life, was a humbling and awe-inspiring experience.

Reflecting on our visit to Mecca, we were struck by the power of faith to bring people together. Despite our differences, we were all connected by our shared devotion to a higher power, in a place that transcends time and space.

Day 4: Lumbini, Nepal
Our final destination was Lumbini, a small town in Nepal that is the birthplace of the Buddha. This pilgrimage site is a place of great spiritual significance, a reminder of the teachings of peace and enlightenment that the Buddha gave to the world.

As we entered the town, we were struck by the peaceful and serene atmosphere. The beautiful gardens and temples here created a sense of tranquility and calm, and we felt a sense of wonder and reverence as we explored.

The highlight of our visit was the Sacred Garden, the site of the Buddha's birthplace. Walking through the quiet paths of the garden, we felt a sense of connection to the Buddha's teachings, and were reminded of the importance of compassion, kindness, and mindfulness.

Reflecting on our visit to Lumbini, we were struck by the simplicity and power of the Buddha's message. In a world of extreme complexity and noise, the Buddha's teachings remind us to slow down, breathe, and connect with the present moment. It was a fitting end to our pilgrimage journey, a reminder of the power and beauty of spiritual connection.

prompt: Write a 3,000 word fantasy short story about a young boy who discovers he is a warlock, incorporating elements of magic, adventure, and danger. The story should have a clear beginning, middle, and end, and the protagonist should encounter and overcome obstacles in their quest to master their newfound powers. Elements of world-building can be included, such as unique magical creatures or spells, but the focus should remain on the character's growth and development. completion:
The sun beat down on the small village of Crestwood, casting a warm blanket over the rolling hills and greenery, and painting the white-capped mountains in the distance with an array of golden and orange hues. It was a perfect day for young boys and girls to explore the outdoors, and for the inhabitants of the village to go about their daily lives. But for one young boy, the day would hold a great surprise, one that would change his life forever.

As he walked through the grassy meadows, kicking up dust and daydreaming about the possibilities of adventure, the boy noticed something strange. A faint whisper in the wind, a rustle in the bushes. He followed the sound and found himself standing before an old tree, its branches twisted and knotted like an ancient hand reaching up from the earth. There was something peculiar about this tree that drew him closer, as if he could sense a palpable energy pulsating from it.

As he got closer, he saw something that made his heart skip a beat. A small rune had been inscribed into the bark, ancient symbols carved into the aged wood. With a sense of curiosity, he traced his fingers over the symbol, feeling a rush of energy coursing through him.

In that moment, the boy realized that he was not just any ordinary boy. He was a warlock. He now had the power to wield magic, to manipulate the very elements themselves.

With newfound excitement coursing through his veins, the boy set out on a journey of discovery, seeking out the knowledge and skills needed to master his abilities. 

As he wandered through the land, he encountered many dangers and obstacles, but nothing could dim his newfound sense of excitement and wonder at the possibilities of magic.

The first obstacle he faced was the challenge of finding a mentor. He knew that he could not master his abilities alone, and so he began searching for someone with knowledge of magic.

He wandered from town to town, seeking out the wise individuals who may have the knowledge he needed. But after months of searching, he found nothing but false leads, charlatans who claimed to be warlocks but refused to teach him the secrets of the trade.

But just as he resolved to give up hope, he stumbled upon a wizard of great renown, a man who claimed to be able to teach him everything he needed to know about magic.

The wizard's name was Arin, and he was a wise and powerful wizard with many years of experience. He agreed to take the boy under his wing, and teach him the ways of the warlock.

Despite his enthusiasm, the boy found the lessons to be rigorous and difficult. The study of magic was not something that could be easily grasped, and he spent many hours laboring over the spells and incantations that Arin taught him.

But just as he felt himself growing more and more frustrated, he began to see the power of his abilities manifesting. The energy he could channel through his body was incredible, and he felt that he was on the cusp of mastering his newfound control over the elements.

With his newly acquired powers, the boy set out once again into the world of adventure, seeking out new challenges and obstacles to overcome.

One day, as he wandered through a dense forest, he encountered a group of dangerous beasts. They were unlike anything he had ever seen before, with skin as hard as steel and fangs as long as his arm.

With his magic at his fingertips, the boy fought valiantly against the creatures, utilizing spells and incantations to conjure powerful attacks and hurl them at his foes. Though the beasts were fearsome, the boy was empowered by his newfound abilities, and he decimated them one by one.

As he emerged victorious over his adversaries, the boy felt a sense of pride and accomplishment that he had never before experienced. He realized that the power of magic was both great and terrible, and that he would have to learn to wield it wisely if he was to survive in this world of danger and mystery.

But the boy knew that he had only just begun to tap into the depth of his abilities. With the knowledge he had gained from Arin, he felt that he could take on anything that the world could throw his way.

And so he set out once again, ready to face whatever challenges lay before him, his heart filled with the wonder and excitement of a young warlock, eager to explore the mysteries of the magical world.

prompt: Provide a comprehensive explanation of the underlying principles, approaches, and techniques applied in the design thinking methodologies utilized in organizations, startups and other settings. Elaborate on the key principles, discuss how they relate to each other, and highlight the importance of each principle in the design thinking process. Provide examples of how design thinking methodologies have been used to identify and solve complex challenges in various industries.
completion:
Design thinking is an approach to problem-solving that aims to address complex challenges using a human-centered approach. It involves a process of ideation, prototyping, and iteration, with a primary focus on the needs of the end-user. The following is a comprehensive explanation of the underlying principles, approaches, and techniques applied in the design thinking methodologies utilized in organizations, startups, and other settings.

Key Principles of Design Thinking
1. Empathy: One of the key principles of design thinking is empathy. Empathy involves having a deep understanding of the users you are designing for, their needs, and their pain points. It is about putting yourself in their shoes and understanding their perspective, thoughts, feelings, and behaviors. Empathy helps designers create solutions that are relevant and meaningful to the users they serve.

2. Iteration: Design thinking is an iterative process. It involves creating, testing, and refining ideas until the best solution emerges. This means that designers are continually testing and refining their ideas as they go, rather than waiting until the end of the design process to make changes. Iteration allows designers to learn from their mistakes, refine their solutions, and ensure that the final output meets the needs of the users.

3. Creativity: Design thinking is a creative process. It involves generating a wide range of ideas and solutions, even ones that might seem unconventional or unusual. Creativity is about breaking down barriers, taking risks, and exploring new possibilities. It helps designers come up with innovative solutions that meet the needs of their users in new and unexpected ways.

4. Collaborative: Design thinking is a collaborative process. It involves working with a team of individuals from different disciplines and backgrounds to create solutions that are both integrated and diverse. Collaboration brings together unique perspectives and diverse skill sets, leading to more creative and effective solutions.

5. Human-Centered: Design thinking is a human-centered approach. It puts the needs of the end-user at the center of the design process. This means that designers aim to understand the needs of their users and create solutions that are intuitive, easy to use, and meet the needs of the end-user.

Approaches and Techniques Applied in Design Thinking
1. Problem Framing: Design Thinking starts by framing the problem you want to solve. A well-defined problem statement ensures that designers can focus on the right challenge and design a solution that meets the users' needs.

2. Research: Designers carry out extensive research to understand the needs, behaviors, and preferences of their users. They need to conduct user interviews, observe behaviors, and conduct surveys to ensure that they have a deep understanding of the problem.

3. Ideation: In ideation, designers generate ideas and brainstorm as many potential solutions as possible. This phase often involves sketching, mind mapping, and other techniques to get the ideas flowing.

4. Prototyping: Prototyping involves creating a quick and cheap solution that can be used to test the viability of the solution. Prototypes can be physical, digital, or a combination of both.

4. Testing: Testing involves gathering feedback from the users and using it to refine and iterate the solution. Designers use feedback to make changes to the prototype to ensure that it meets the needs of the users.

Examples of how design thinking methodologies have been used to identify and solve complex challenges in various industries
1. Healthcare: Design thinking has been used in healthcare to develop new medical devices, improve patient experience, and develop new treatment options. For example, Stanford’s Institute of Design collaborated with the Mayo Clinic to improve patient experience and created a new concept for a hospital room.

2. Education: Design thinking has been used in education to improve teaching methods and learning experiences. For example, a group of teachers in Singapore used design thinking to develop new teaching methods that align with the needs of the students.

3. ECommerce: Design thinking has been used in eCommerce to improve the user experience, reduce cart abandonment rates, and increase sales. Amazon uses design thinking to experiment with new product strategies, implement innovations, and improve its digital products.

4. Financial services: Design thinking has been used to improve financial services and develop new products that meet the needs of the customers. For example, Spanish banking giant BBVA used design thinking to design a new mobile banking app that is user-friendly, intuitive, and meets the needs of its customers.

In conclusion, design thinking is an essential part of problem-solving in various industries. Its principles, approaches, and techniques have been proven effective in identifying and solving complex challenges. Design thinking allows designers to create solutions that are user-centered, creative, and collaborative. By applying these methodologies, organizations and startups can innovate and develop solutions that meet the needs of their users.

prompt: Write a fictional short story, between 1000 and 1500 words, about a high-powered executive who must decide between keeping their dream job or leaving it to prioritize their family. Consider exploring the protagonist's motives, personal and professional relationships, and the potential consequences of their decision. Use descriptive language and character development to create a compelling narrative with a clear conflict and resolution.
completion:
Carla was a high-powered executive at a top advertising firm. She had worked tirelessly to get to where she was in her career, sacrificing time with family and friends to climb the corporate ladder. She had always been ambitious, and her success had only fueled her drive further.

But lately, Carla had started to feel a nagging sense of dissatisfaction. She missed spending time with her husband and children, and she felt like she was missing out on their lives. Her job kept her constantly busy, and even when she was at home, she found it difficult to switch off and be present with her family.

One day, Carla's husband, Mark, sat her down for a serious talk. He told her that he couldn't keep up with her lifestyle anymore, that their children needed her more than she needed her job. Carla was taken aback; she had never considered giving up her career, the job that she had worked so hard for, and that she loved so much.

Over the next few days, Carla couldn't stop thinking about what Mark had said. She loved her family, but she also loved her job. She thrived on the pressure, the adrenaline rush that came with meeting tight deadlines and pushing creative boundaries. But she also knew that her family needed her, that she was missing out on precious moments with her husband and children.

Carla sought advice from her closest friends and colleagues, but none of them could offer her the answers she was looking for. She had to figure it out on her own.

Finally, she made a decision. She would take a few weeks off work and spend some quality time with her family. Maybe that would help her make up her mind.

The next few weeks were a blur of family time, laughter, and happy moments. Carla realized how much she had missed this, how much she had been craving it without even knowing it. But still, there was a restlessness inside of her, a nagging sense of not being fulfilled. She missed work, missed the thrill of the job.

One day, during a family outing, Carla received an urgent call from her boss. One of their biggest clients had pulled out of a major project, and the deadline was fast approaching. They needed Carla's help, her expertise, her creativity.

Without thinking, Carla jumped at the opportunity. She told her family she had to work, but promised to make it up to them. And for the next few days, she worked tirelessly on the project, putting in long hours, skipping meals and sleep, but enjoying every moment of it.

Finally, the project was done, and it was a resounding success. Carla felt proud, fulfilled, and happy. But when she returned home, she found her family sitting at the table, looking at her with sad eyes.

"Mom," her youngest daughter said, tears in her eyes. "Why do you love your job more than us?"

Carla felt like she had been hit with a sledgehammer. She had always known that her family came first, yet somehow, she had let her ambition get the better of her. She realized that if she didn't make a change now, she risked losing her family forever.

That night, Carla made a decision. She would leave her job and prioritize her family. It was a tough choice, but it felt like the right one. She knew that it wouldn't be easy, that her career would take a hit, that she would miss the hustle and bustle of the job. But she also knew that her family needed her, that she needed them just as much.

Carla's boss was shocked when she told him that she was quitting. He begged her to stay, offered her double her current salary, promised her anything she wanted. But Carla was resolute. She thanked him for everything he had done for her, for giving her the opportunity to do what she loved, but she knew where her priorities lay.

It wasn't an easy transition, but Carla made it work. She started her own advertising agency, one that allowed her to work from home, to be present for her family, yet still fulfill her creative drive. And as her agency grew, so did her family, stronger and happier than ever before.

Looking back, Carla realized that she had been chasing the wrong dream all along. Her true dream had been to balance work and family, to live a life of purpose, of happiness, of love. And she had finally found it.

As she watched her children playing in the backyard, with her husband by her side, Carla knew that she had made the right decision. It wasn't easy, but it was worth it. And that was all that mattered.

prompt: Write a horror story of at least 1000 words about a family who moves into a new home, only to discover that it is built on top of an ancient burial ground. Your story should include descriptive language and vivid imagery. You may incorporate elements of suspense, terror, or gore as you see fit, but the focus should be on building a sense of palpable dread as the family confronts the malevolent spirits that have been awakened by their presence. Be sure to include a satisfying resolution that draws the story to a close while still leaving readers with a lingering sense of unease.
completion:
The Smith family was excited to move into their new home. The house was big, beautiful and had everything that they needed. However, they were not aware that their new home was built on an ancient burial ground. They didn't know that they were about to face a nightmare that they might never forget.

The first night in their new home was like any other first night in a new place - they were all excited, restless and couldn't wait to explore every corner of their new home. The house was quiet and calm, and everyone was sleeping soundly until they heard a loud noise coming from downstairs. 

Mr. Smith got up and went to check it out. The door was open, and he found footprints on the floor. He had a bad feeling about it and locked the door before going back to bed. As soon as his head hit the pillow, he heard whispers coming from the corner of the room that were unintelligible yet very real.

The next day, the family decided to explore the local town, and they went to the library to learn more about their home's history. They were shocked to learn that there was an ancient burial ground below their house. The librarian shared stories about how the burial ground was cursed, and people who had dug up the corpses in the past had experienced terrible misfortune.

The family was also informed that the spirits buried beneath their house were disturbed and angry. The Smiths were terrified, but they tried to act normal, thinking that it was just a myth. They were completely unprepared for what was to come.

The first night had been just an introduction to what was about to happen. Every night thereafter was more horrific than the previous. They would hear whispers, crying, and footsteps. They could feel the presence of someone or something in their home. The air was always heavy, and every breath they took became labored. The family started sleeping with the lights on, hoping it would keep the spirits at bay. 

One night, the family woke up to the sound of the doors opening and closing. They all knew that it couldn't be the wind or anyone in the house, as it was pitch black inside. Smoke started to fill their rooms, and the smell of ashes mixed with the air. It was as if someone had set fire to the house. 

The family ran outside, and as they looked back, they saw the flames engulfing the house. The fire department arrived quickly, but it was too late. Everything was burnt to ashes.

The Smith family was now homeless, and they had nothing left. They visited the library again and asked for more information about the burial ground. The librarian informed them that the spirits were not happy, and they had plans to revenge. The Smiths had taken their land, built their home over their burial ground, and disturbed their rest. These spirits had been wronged, and they would not rest until the Smiths were gone.

The family realized that they were running out of options. They decided to ask a well-known psychic medium for help. The medium told them that the spirits needed to be sent back to their resting place. She informed them that they had to offer a sacrifice to appease the spirits. The Smiths were horrified, but they did not have any other options. 

They bought a goat and offered it to the spirits. As soon as they placed the goat on top of the burial ground, they could hear murmurs, whispers, and cries. The medium chanted as the spirits took the sacrifice. As she finished, they heard a deep sigh, and the ground shook.

The family went back to their new home, and to their surprise, it was as if nothing had happened. There was no smoke, no whispers, no footsteps and no sense of dread. They knew that the ritual they had performed had worked. The spirits were at peace, and they could now rest. 

The family knew they had to leave that place, that house. But they didn't do it immediately. The experience had changed them, and they lived with the burden of what they had done and the realization that the dead could be very much alive, and very much angry. 

The Smiths finally moved away, but they were changed forever. They knew that the spirits would always remember them as those who dared to disturb their peace. They would never forget, and always be watching. The family promised themselves and each other that they would never, ever disturb the peace of any burial ground or ancient resting place, ever again.

Question/Instruction: Can a single-member LLC protect the company from personal liabilities?

Given material: 1 Do You Need to Name Your Wife on the LLC?

3 Does a Single-Member LLC Need a Board of Directors?
An LLC, or limited-liability company, is a legal entity for a business that provides much of the same liability protection for its owners as a corporation would without actually being a corporation. The specific statutes for single- and multi-member LLCs vary from state to state. However, an understanding of general trends can help you to decide whether you and your spouse should both be listed as members of the LLC.
In some cases, only one spouse may have any actual involvement in the running of the LLC, while the other may intend to remain completely uninvolved. In these cases, it may seem natural to adopt the single-member LLC model. However, if a husband and wife agree that they prefer to get any added protection that a multi-member LLC can offer, they may find it worthwhile to adopt a multi-member LLC model. In this case, the second member should be able to show at least some level of involvement in the company's operations and decisions. Otherwise, according to Keyt Law, a court may later define her as a "sham member" and rule that the LLC is a single-member LLC.
While single-member and multi-member LLCs tend to provide the same level of protection of personal assets from company liabilities, the same cannot be said for protecting the company from personal liabilities. For instance, in a Chapter 7 bankruptcy case, the court has the power to seize many types of assets belonging to the person who has declared bankruptcy.
If an LLC is a multi-member LLC, this seizure of assets usually cannot extend to company assets without the consent of the LLC other members, as it would essentially result in the court taking one person's assets due to another person's bankruptcy. However, in a single-member LLC, the court may view company assets as being synonymous with owner assets, seizing anything valuable owned by the company to sell it off and pay the owner's debts.
When married couples file for divorce, they often go to court regarding the partition of assets. An LLC can be a very valuable asset. If one spouse owns a single-member LLC, the other spouse might be entitled to all or a portion of that LLC's assets. This decision is something that occurs on a case-by-case basis after a fair amount of litigation.
However, in the case of a multi-member LLC, the operating agreement should specifically stipulate the amount of the company that each member owns. In this case, the court may simply rule that each spouse remains with the share of the business apportioned in the operating agreement.
In the United States, corporate income is often double-taxed in that both the company and the shareholders must pay income tax. LLCs, on the other hand, only have their income taxed on the owner's level. For this reason, on the company level, no difference exists between single- and multi-member LLCs when it comes to income taxation.
However, on the personal level, a married couple may see a difference when it comes to taxation of personal income. If a married couple files separate tax returns and only one spouse owns the LLC, the profits from the LLC may put that individual into a higher tax bracket, resulting in a higher tax rate. If a married couple files a joint tax return under a single-member LLC or if both spouses are members of the LLC, this may not happen.
Limited Liability Company Center: Single Member LLC or Multiple Member LLC?

Read the passage below and answer the question or follow the instruction: What role does the policy of other countries like China, Russia, or South Korea play in the negotiations with North Korea?

Passage: The ink is barely dry on the joint statement signed by President Trump and North Korean leader Kim Jong Un during Tuesday's summit in Singapore, and yet people are already dumping on it. This is no "deal," the critics say. It's just a vague press release rehashing talking points.
But on the whole, the meeting is an auspicious start.
A follow-up press conference announced some concrete steps: The U.S. Would halt military exercises in South Korea, Kim apparently agreed not only to the principle of denuclearization, but to some sort of inspection regime, and Trump announced a follow-up meeting between Secretary of State Mike Pompeo and a North Korean counterpart. Still, there's no mention of a peace treaty — North Korea and the U.S. Are still technically at war — or a deadline, or many other specifics.
But there was never any realistic expectation that a single meeting between two men could produce a comprehensive deal. For starters, a comprehensive deal would have to include China, Russia, and South Korea. And, of course, there will be details to be ironed out. President Ronald Reagan's historic Reykjavik summit with Mikhail Gorbachev — the obvious template for what Trump is trying to do with Kim — happened in 1986, and the resulting Intermediate-Range Nuclear Forces Treaty only happened in 1987.
The point of such summits is not to come out with a full treaty neatly packaged and tied with a bow. It is to build rapport between leaders — which matters enormously — and get a sense of each side's red lines, which will form the outlines of a future deal.
Right now, there is so much we don't know. Trump will say anything. Kim is also a complete mystery. Perhaps, being from a different generation and having been exposed to the outside world before joining the family business, Kim has a genuine desire to open up his country, if only because it would make him much richer and enable him to travel a lot more. Or perhaps he is just dangling the possibility of a comprehensive deal in front of an all-too-gullible U.S. President to get short-term relief on aid and trade, with no intention of actually denuclearizing, a game that his father was quite adept at. Your guess is as good as mine. Besides, every single international summit ends with the parties pretending it's been a big success, regardless of the actual contents.
With all those caveats duly noted, it certainly seems like the summit's goals have been accomplished. Trump and Kim do seem to have built real rapport, and the peace process with North Korea seems more alive now than at any point since the 1990s. If Kim's desire to reach a settlement is genuine, and if Trump manages not to screw it up, a good deal could be in sight. I agree those are very big ifs, but every international negotiation of consequence includes very large ifs, and that was true before Trump. In other words, there's reason to be cautiously optimistic. Given what could be realistically accomplished in one day, it's hard not to think that if anybody other than Trump were president, the summit would immediately have been hailed a preliminary success.
And really, credit needs to be given where it's due. It does seem like it was Trump's contempt for conventional thinking, and his dealmaking instincts, that got us here. The official U.S. Policy was to refuse these kinds of meetings unless there were major concessions from the North Koreans, as these would grant North Korea "legitimacy." That policy seems to have simply alienated North Korea's leadership. Thinking like a real estate developer, Trump understood that giving Kim a photo-op costs him nothing. Besides, such "legitimacy" matters little for a regime that, domestically, controls all of its media and can therefore manufacture it at will, and internationally has pretty clearly accepted its rogue status. Simple-mindedness can be destructive, but it can also mean you see the forest for the trees. Trump blithely cut to the heart of the issue at hand: Does Kim want normalization badly enough that he's willing to give up his nukes?
It looks like Trump is well on his way to finding out the answer to that question. And whatever the outcome, we should all be grateful for it.

The missing person should be a young woman with a mysterious past, and there should be several twists and turns as the investigation unfolds. completion:
Title: The Case of the Missing Girl

Cast:
Sheriff Dale
Retired detective Joe
Local storekeeper Tim
Town gossip Jane
Missing girl Lily

Setting: A small town in the Midwest

Act I:

Scene 1:
A small town in the Midwest. The stage is set up to look like a sheriff’s office. The town’s sheriff, Dale, sits at his desk, filling out some paperwork. He peers up as the door opens, revealing Tim, the local storekeeper.

Dale: Hello, Tim. What brings you here?

Tim: Well, I heard you were looking for that missing girl, Lily. I thought I might be able to help.

Dale: Sure, Tim. We could use all the help we can get.

Scene 2:
Dale and Tim are discussing the case in the sheriff’s office when Retired Detective Joe walks in.

Joe: Hello, boys. Mind if I join you?

Dale: Not at all, Joe. We could use some fresh perspective on this case.

Tim: You detectives sure know how to solve a mystery.

Joe: Well, I’ve been retired for a while now. But I suppose I can give it a shot.

Scene 3:
Later that same day, the town’s gossip, Jane, walks into the sheriff’s office. Dale rolls his eyes but lets her in.

Jane: Oh, Sheriff! Have you found Lily yet? I heard she was kidnapped by aliens!

Dale: Come on, Jane. We’re not dealing with aliens here.

Jane: Well, I heard it from a reliable source! You know I’m always on the case when it comes to juicy gossip.

Act II:

Scene 1:
The investigation is in full swing, and they’ve uncovered some new leads. They gather in Joe’s office to discuss.

Joe: Alright, boys. I’ve been doing some digging around, and I’ve got a theory.

Dale: What is it, Joe?

Joe: I think Lily might have been involved with some shady characters in the past. Maybe they caught up with her.

Tim: You mean like a drug dealer or something?

Joe: Exactly.

Dale: I’ll put out an APB on known drug dealers in the area.

Scene 2:
The investigation leads them to a run-down cabin just outside of town. They gather around the cabin, guns drawn.

Dale: Alright, boys. Let’s do this.

They break down the door and rush in, only to find the cabin empty.

Joe: Damn it! They must have gotten away.

Tim: What do we do now?

Dale: We keep searching. We’ll find her.

Scene 3:
Finally, they get a break in the case. A local resident comes forward, saying they saw a young woman matching Lily’s description get into a car with a man they didn’t recognize.

Dale: Alright, boys. Let’s go find this guy.

They race off, sirens blaring.

Act III:

Scene 1:

Dale: Alright, everyone, be on high alert.

prompt: Write a classic mystery novel about a seasoned detective who investigates a string of high-profile robberies at a prestigious jewelry store in the heart of the city, while facing both personal and professional obstacles along the way. Incorporate rich character development, atmospheric descriptions, and a clever plot twist that will keep readers guessing until the very end.
completion:
Chapter 1:

Detective Miles Brown had seen it all. After over 20 years with the NYPD, he had dealt with every type of criminal there was. But this case was different. It was personal.

He stood outside the prestigious jewelry store on Madison Avenue, watching as the forensic team dusted for fingerprints and took photographs of the smashed display cases. This was the fifth robbery at the store in the past six months, and each time the thief had managed to evade capture.

Brown had been assigned to the case, and he was determined to crack it. He surveyed the scene, taking in the details. The thief had smashed the cases with a sledgehammer, but had taken only the most valuable pieces - diamonds, emeralds, and rubies worth over $10 million in total.

As he studied the scene, Brown felt a sense of unease. The case was beginning to get under his skin. He had a feeling that this was more than just a simple robbery.

Chapter 2:

Brown's suspicions were confirmed when he received a call from an anonymous informant a few days later. The informant claimed to know the identity of the thief responsible for the string of jewelry store robberies.

Brown was skeptical at first, but the informant seemed to have inside knowledge that only someone involved with the theft could know. Brown arranged to meet with him in a secluded park in the city to gather more information.

As Brown waited for the informant to arrive, he couldn't help but think about the case. The thief had planned each robbery meticulously, leaving no evidence behind. Brown had interviewed multiple suspects and had even used surveillance footage from nearby buildings, but each lead had turned up empty.

When the informant finally arrived, he revealed that the thief was a local millionaire named Richard Reynolds. Reynolds had a history of shady dealings and had recently fallen on hard times. The informant claimed that Reynolds had stolen the jewelry to sell on the black market to pay off his debts.

Brown was shocked by the revelation. Reynolds had always seemed like an upstanding citizen. But the evidence was there - Reynolds had motive, opportunity, and insider knowledge of the security at the jewelry store.

Chapter 3:

With this new information, Brown set out to gather enough evidence to arrest Reynolds. He worked tirelessly, poring over financial records and interviewing Reynolds' business associates. But every time he thought he had enough evidence, it slipped through his grasp.

Brown was becoming obsessed with the case. He was neglecting his family and friends, focusing all his attention on Reynolds. And the more he dug, the more he realized that Reynolds was not acting alone. There were other wealthy individuals involved in the thefts, each with their own reasons for wanting the jewelry.

As the investigation dragged on, Brown began to feel like he was losing his grip on reality. He was working nonstop, sleeping only a few hours a night, and he was haunted by the image of the stolen jewelry. He became convinced that the jewelry was cursed, and that it was leading him down a dangerous path.

Chapter 4:

Finally, after months of tireless work, Brown had gathered enough evidence to indict Reynolds and his associates. The trial was a media circus, with reporters from all over the city flocking to the courthouse to cover the proceedings.

As the evidence piled up against Reynolds, Brown began to feel a sense of relief. He had finally solved the case that had consumed him for so long. But there was still one piece of evidence that didn't quite add up - a necklace that had been recovered from Reynolds' safe.

Brown had studied the necklace extensively, and had determined that it was worth over $1 million. But there was something strange about it. It was a unique design, one that he had never seen before. And as he examined it further, he noticed something else - a small engraving on the clasp.

The engraving read "To Miles, with love."

Chapter 5:

The realization hit Brown like a ton of bricks. The necklace was a gift from his wife, who he had neglected during the investigation. She had left him a year ago, taking their daughter with her.

Brown had been so consumed with the case that he had not realized what was right in front of him. He had lost his family, his friends, and his sanity in his quest for justice.

As the trial wrapped up, Brown made a decision. He would leave the force and try to rebuild his life. He knew that the jewelry would be returned to the store, and that life would go on. But he also knew that he would never be the same person again.

In the end, justice had been served. But at what cost?

prompt: Write a 750-word article explaining the role of mentorship in fostering a successful business environment. Discuss the benefits of mentorship programs, including leadership development and increased employee retention rates. Use real-world examples to illustrate the impact of mentorship and offer practical tips for both mentors and mentees to maximize learning opportunities. Additionally, provide insight into the qualities of a good mentor and how to establish an effective mentor-mentee relationship. Your article should balance informative content with engaging writing style and appropriate tone.
completion:
In today's competitive business world, mentorship programs have become increasingly important for fostering a successful environment. These programs allow experienced professionals to share their knowledge and expertise with younger employees, helping them develop the skills they need to succeed both personally and professionally. In this article, we will discuss the benefits of mentorship programs and provide practical tips for both mentors and mentees to maximize learning opportunities.

Leadership Development
One of the main benefits of mentorship programs is leadership development. When experienced professionals mentor younger employees, they help them develop their leadership skills, which is essential for running a successful business. Mentors share their own leadership experiences, offering invaluable advice and guidance on how to handle challenging situations. Mentees learn about the importance of delegating tasks, managing a team, problem-solving, and decision-making. Such skills are not only vital in the workplace but also for personal growth.

Increased Employee Retention Rates
Mentorship programs also contribute to increased employee retention rates. When younger employees feel like they have a mentor who is invested in their success, they are more likely to stay with the company for the long term. A recent study showed that employees who have mentors are 130% more likely to be promoted to higher positions than those who do not have mentors. Additionally, the same study revealed that companies with mentorship programs had a 70% higher retention rate than companies without mentorship programs.

Real-World Examples
Several real-world examples demonstrate the impact of mentorship programs in fostering a successful business environment. For instance, Microsoft has a mentorship program, that is part of its leadership development initiative. The program matches employees with mentors who are experienced professionals in a similar field. The relationship between the mentor and mentee includes one-on-one meetings, job shadowing, and other activities aimed at enhancing leadership skills. As a result, Microsoft has seen an improvement in employee retention rates and the development of its leaders.

Another example is General Electric's (GE) "reverse mentoring" program, which targets senior executives who are paired with junior employees. The program aims to help senior executives understand the perspective of younger employees and gain insight into novel technologies and emerging trends. This program has helped GE embrace digital transformation and implement innovative technologies that have contributed to the success of the company.

Tips For Mentors
Mentors play a critical role in the success of mentorship programs, and as such, there are several tips for mentors to maximize learning opportunities. Firstly, mentors should establish clear expectations for the relationship from the get-go, including the communication frequency, availability, and preferred communication methods. Secondly, mentors should be open-minded and empathetic, listening to their mentee's concerns and offering constructive feedback. Thirdly, mentors should be proactive and initiate meetings, suggesting relevant learning opportunities, and check on their mentee's progress regularly.

Tips For Mentees
On the other hand, there are specific tips that mentees should consider to make the most of mentorship programs. Firstly, mentees should be receptive to feedback and be willing to learn from their mentor's experience. Secondly, mentees should be transparent with their mentor about their career goals, aspirations, and areas they would like to improve. Thirdly, mentees should ask questions and be forthcoming with requests for learning opportunities and feedback.

Qualities Of A Good Mentor
Several qualities differentiate good mentors from others, and they include empathy, experience, and excellent communication skills. Empathy enables a mentor to understand and appreciate their mentee's perspective, facilitating effective communication. In terms of experience, a good mentor should have a wealth of knowledge and experience that they can share with their mentee. Lastly, effective communication skills are core to establishing and sustaining a mentor-mentee relationship.

Establishing An Effective Mentor-Mentee Relationship
Establishing a successful mentor-mentee relationship requires concerted effort and commitment from both parties. To start with, both parties should recognize the need for a mentorship program and be eager to participate fully. Secondly, both parties should be proactive and establish clear expectations for the relationship to ensure that communication is transparent and consistent. Lastly, both parties should embrace feedback, be open-minded and receptive to learning opportunities.

In conclusion, mentorship programs play a crucial role in fostering a successful business environment, enhancing leadership skills, and improving employee retention rates. Real-world examples show the significant impact of mentorship programs, and practical tips for mentors and mentees offer insight into how to maximize learning opportunities. The qualities of a good mentor and an effective mentor-mentee relationship are essential to ensure that the program is beneficial to both parties.

prompt: Write a minimum of 500 words descriptive essay incorporating sensory details about a fictional location of your choice using the prompt "A place I've never been". Make sure to organize your essay effectively with a clear introduction, body paragraphs that use strong, vivid language to convey your sensory experience, and a conclusion that leaves a lasting impression on your reader. Consider utilizing comparisons or metaphors to further enhance your description. Lastly, avoid using cliches and ensure that your essay is unique and engaging.
completion:
As I stepped out of the airport, the fragrant aroma of sweet spices and exotic fruits flooded my senses. I was finally in Marrakech, a place I've never been before. My eyes widened at the bustling scene before me, and I felt the warmth of the sun on my skin. It was unlike any other place I had ever been.

I stepped into the heart of the city, Marrakech's Medina, and was greeted by narrow alleyways filled with colourful markets and the sound of haggling. The vibrant colours of the stalls were a sensory overload; beautiful tapestries hung from the walls, lanterns in bold reds and blues hung from the ceilings, and the sweet smell of incense and candle wax filled the air. In the background, I heard the beautiful melodies of Middle Eastern music, with the rhythm of the instruments instantly making my feet start to tap.

The sound of a bustling market surrounded me as I walked through the Medina, taking in the sights and smells of the vendors' fresh produce. Stalls were piled high with fresh fruits and vegetables; oranges, lemons and limes that looked vibrant and juicy against the hazy skyline. Grapes were stacked high in wooden boxes, and I could smell the sweetness of the fruit from a distance. Piles of fresh spices lined the stalls too; pepper, cinnamon, nutmeg and cardamom all mixing together to create an otherworldly scent. The spice vendors' brightly coloured spices were so visually appealing that I found myself torn between the delicious scent or the beautiful sight before me.

As I left the market behind, the call to prayer echoed loudly across the tranquil city. I paused, taking in the sound of the chanting and the hauntingly beautiful melody. I felt a sense of peace wash over me as I listened, knowing that it was the start of the day's religious rituals. The stark contrast between the lively market and the silence during prayer was an awe-inspiring moment of reflection.

The streets of Marrakech continue to lead me on through the city— the desert colours of the buildings, with rich oranges and deep yellows emanating a sense of warmth around me. The architecture throughout the city felt inviting, with its arched doorways, tiled roofs, and intricate details, which give the city a distinct character. The soundscape of Marrakech was so different to anything I had ever experienced before, from the hypnotic sounds of the snake charmers, to the chatter of the vendors making the sounds of the streets truly unique.

As I continued my exploration of Marrakech, I wandered through the pearly gates of the Bahia Palace. The intricately carved arabesque walls and ceilings, the marble courtyards, and water-filled channels alongside the tiled fountains filled my senses. As I walked through the palace, I could feel the cool tiles underfoot that were thankfully out of direct sunlight. The smell of flowers being cultivated in the gardens mixed with the soundscape to create a peaceful oasis in the bustling city. It was a serene reminder of the beauty beyond the city's walls and the moments I could cherish forever.

At last, I arrived at the magnificent Koutoubia Mosque. The mosque was the largest in Marrakech, and it rose proudly into the sky, with a distinctive minaret and the crescent-topped roof that instantly catches the eye. The sound of the mihrab, the prayer niche set into the wall pointing towards Mecca, alongside the prayers from congregants only adding to the immersive experience. The simple elegance and history of the site made it truly breathtaking.

As the sun set on Marrakech, I sat on a rooftop terrace, taking in the breathtaking view overlooking the Medina. The skyline was awash with the golden hues of sunset, with the calls to prayer filling the air once again. The oranges and pinks of the sky visible through the softly shimmering heat haze were breathtaking. I couldn't have foreseen the sublime sensory experience that Marrakech had offered me.

In conclusion, Marrakech was a sensory feast for the eyes, nose, and ears throughout my visit. The colours of the markets, the sounds of the call to prayer, and the beauty of landmarks such as the Koutoubia Mosque will forever stay etched in my memory. The city was a blending of cultures, architecture and colours unlike anything else found around the world. Despite being a place I've never been, Marrakech created an unforgettable sensory experience that I'll cherish forever.

prompt: Write a 45-minute realistic drama script about a middle-class American family of four struggling to cope with the heroin addiction of their eldest son, including scenes of intervention, hospitalization, and relapse. Ensure that the dialogue feels natural and authentic, with each family member having a unique perspective and voice, and that the plot explores the emotional toll of addiction on the individual and the family dynamic. The script should be suitable for a small stage production, with minimal sets and props required.
completion:
Title: Shattered Dreams

Charcaters:

- John (40s) - The father
- Amy (40s) - The mother
- Jack (20s) - The oldest son
- Ben (teenage) - The youngest son

Scene 1: Jack's Confession
(Afternoon. The family is seated in the living room. Jack looks anxious)

John: What's up, Jack? You're looking nervous.

Amy: Is everything alright, son?

Jack: (nervously) Mom, Dad, I have something to tell you. Something important.

John: Don't beat around the bush, Jack. Just spit it out.

Jack: (hesitates for a moment) I've been struggling with heroin addiction for some time now, and I can't do it alone anymore.

(Amy gasps while John looks crestfallen)

Amy: (tearfully) Oh, Jack, why didn't you tell us earlier? We could have helped you!

John: (firmly) How long have you been using, Jack?

Jack: (faltering) A year or so, I think.

Ben: (shocked) How could we not know about it?

Amy: (solemnly) Addiction is a disease that can remain hidden for a long time.

John: (sighs heavily) We have to do something about this.

Scene 2: The Intervention
(Night. The family is holding an intervention for Jack at their home)

John: Jack, we love you and care about you. You need to look at yourself and the life you're living. You're not alone in this struggle, and we're here to help you get through it.

Amy: (sympathetically) We've talked to a therapist, and we think it's best if you enter rehab.

Jack: (angrily) I don't need rehab! I can do this on my own!

Ben: (concerned) Jack, please don't make things harder for yourself. It's okay to ask for help.

(After some arguing, Jack finally agrees to enter rehab)

Scene 3: At the Rehab Center
(A week later. Jack is seen talking to the therapist while the family waits outside)

John: (impatiently) What's taking so long?

Amy: (reassuringly) It's a process, John. Let's give him some space and time to heal.

(As they wait, Jack comes out of the therapist's office)

Jack: (sobbing) Guys, I'm so sorry for everything I've put you through. I want to change, and I need your support.

Amy: (hugging him) We're here for you, Jack. We love you.

John: (smiling) We're proud of you for taking this step, son. Let's get you better.

Scene 4: Relapse
(A few months later. Jack has completed rehab and is back home)

Ben: (excitedly) Jack, I missed you so much! You look great!

Jack: (smiling) It's good to be back.

(A week later, Jack is nowhere to be found)

Amy: (worriedly) He's not picking up his phone. I'm afraid he's using again.

John: (angrily) I can't believe he's thrown everything away after working hard to get better.

(The family finds Jack unconscious in his bedroom, having overdosed on heroin)

Amy: (tearfully) We have to take him to the hospital.

John: (firmly) This is it, Jack. You need to understand that this addiction is not a game. It can kill you.

(The family is seen waiting anxiously in the hospital while Jack is undergoing treatment. Jack is eventually released from the hospital)

Being in contact with a big network of local anglers keeps me well informed about how the fishing is going. Without exception, all the latest reports tell of some of the leanest and toughest days on the water in recent times.
Sometimes telling it the way it is makes for a fairly ugly report. Still, I’m going to give it to you warts and all! There are a few nice bream captures to talk about, but the lack of fish being caught is the feature of this month’s report. Recent rainfall and the resulting floods are a major cause of the lack of fish.
As everyone knows by now, East Gippsland finally got the big dump of rain it needed, and there has now been considerable follow-up rain as well. All the rivers into the Gippy Lakes have been flood affected. At last the terrible dry spell has definitely broken, in this part of the world at least. It’s often said it takes a flood to break a drought! The down side is that with all the dirty water about, estuary fishing will now take a back seat at least for the immediate future.
Another great run of big bream showed up in early winter and, after the last few rain events, they should now be flushed right out of the rivers and into the lakes. Usually mid-October and November, when the fish start spawning, is when we see them move back into the rivers. I know that bait anglers using prawn or shrimp have found a few bream to 1kg in the Nicholson and Tambo rivers, but generally the bait boys have been fairly quiet.
It’s the lure anglers that have been really cleaning up. Special mention goes to Anthony Havers who has had some awesome sport, returning plenty of thumper bream to 44cm. Using soft plastics, he has been fishing deep and slow while stacking up 10–20 fish on each of his last six days on the water. He absolutely swears by the Gulp! lures, and the 4 inch Worm or 3 inch Minnow are his favourites.
Another great effort came from Rick Morrison. He went and braved the local dirty rivers between the heavy rain and fished sandworms in the fast flowing, chocolate coloured waters. Incredibly he pulled two thumper bream over 40cm, proving there’s no stopping the keenest anglers even in filthy flooded water! Both fish were released.
In a few outings before the rains with a good mate of mine, Chris Burbidge, we experimented with our newfound addiction of sight casting to bream. Searching the clear water of the lakes over the last few years has opened up an exciting and at times challenging way to lure for bream. We cruise the endless shallows of the lake edges until we spy on our quarry, then cautiously flick lightly-weighted lures to the fish.
Some bream race over and gobble up just about anything we put in front of them. Other cranky customers spook in a hurry, as if we had dropped a bomb on the water. Most of the time, inquisitive bream amble over and inspect our hard-bodied lures – and more often than not just swim away without any further interest. Some will follow right up to the boat and charge off just before the lure is pulled out of the water. This does get you rather frustrated, but the few fish that we actually trick and hook up to makes it all worthwhile.
On the rare occasion, a bream will materialise from nowhere and before you know it you’re hooked up and watching it shake its head trying to rattle the lure free. Regardless of how it happens, actually seeing and observing bream at the point of hook up is so much fun. On our last day out we tallied up eight fish each, from 34–40cm, and while we didn’t break any records, we certainly went home smiling.
Now for the not so good news. After the recent floods, the estuary fishing scene has been turned upside down and it will take a long time to recover. It was the downpour we needed, though, and the floods of 2007 will go down in history as a real drought-breaking event that put water back into our thirsty dams. In the long run, the Gippy Lakes will only benefit from the big input of fresh water.
