prompt: Create a comprehensive how-to guide detailing specific techniques and strategies for enhancing communication skills among colleagues, supervisors, and subordinates in a professional environment. Cover topics such as active listening, assertiveness, conflict resolution, body language, and effective feedback delivery. Use clear and concise language and provide practical examples to help readers understand and implement the recommendations. Additionally, consider tailoring the guide to specific roles or departments within the workplace to make it more relevant and applicable to readers.
completion:
Introduction:

Effective communication is an essential skill that employees must possess to excel in any professional environment. The ability to communicate effectively involves both listening and speaking skills, often working together to convey the intended message.

This guide will explore a range of techniques and strategies for enhancing communication skills among colleagues, supervisors, and subordinates in a professional environment. It will focus on topics such as active listening, assertiveness, conflict resolution, body language, and effective feedback delivery. By developing these essential skills, you can build stronger relationships, resolve disputes, and elevate your professional profile.

Active Listening:

Active listening is the act of fully concentrating on what the speaker is saying, understanding the message, and responding appropriately. It is one of the most critical components of communication and helps to build better rapport and relationships between individuals.

To improve your active listening skills, follow the following techniques:

1. Give your full attention: Give your undivided attention to the speaker. Put away any distractions like phones or anything that will divert your attention.

2. Avoid interrupting the speaker: Wait until the speaker has finished speaking before making your point. You can note down what you want to say while the speaker is talking.

3. Repeat what you heard: Paraphrasing what you heard the speaker say can help you confirm that you are correctly understanding the message.

4. Ask relevant questions: Asking questions based on the speaker's message can also help you understand the message clearly.

Assertiveness:

Assertiveness is the ability to communicate your needs, wants, and opinions effectively, without infringing on other people's rights. Assertive communication enables you to maintain your self-respect, build valuable relationships and resolve conflicts more effectively.

To become more assertive, follow the following techniques:

1. Use "I" statements: Communicate how you feel about an issue or situation by using "I" statements, which help to reduce defensiveness and resentment.

2. Be clear and direct: Avoid ambiguity and be straightforward in your communication.

3. Respect others: While you communicate your thoughts, remember to respect others and their opinions.

4. Compromise where possible: If a conflict arises, look for ways to compromise to find a resolution that satisfies both parties.

Conflict Resolution:

Conflict resolution is the process of resolving disagreements or disputes between colleagues, supervisors, and subordinates. When conflicts occur, it can lead to a negative impact on productivity, job satisfaction, and, ultimately, the bottom line.

To resolve conflicts, follow the following techniques:

1. Identify the issue: Define the problem or issue that requires resolution.

2. Listen to all parties: Gather all relevant parties and listen to each side to obtain all perspectives of the issue.

3. Find common ground: Identify areas of agreement between the parties that can form the basis for an acceptable resolution.

4. Propose solutions: Propose solutions that address the identified issue and that all parties agree upon.

Body Language:

Non-verbal communication, such as body language, can have a profound impact on the effectiveness of your communication skills. Being aware of how you present yourself can help you convey the right message and maintain positive communication.

To improve body language, follow the following techniques:

1. Maintain eye contact: Make and maintain eye contact when communicating. This can convey confidence and interest.

2. Be aware of your posture: Stand or sit up straight, maintaining an open and relaxed posture to convey confidence and credibility.

3. Smile: Smiling can convey friendliness and warmth.

4. Monitor your gestures: Be aware of the non-verbal cues you may be sending to others through your movements.

Effective Feedback Delivery:

Providing feedback is crucial for growth and development in a professional environment. Giving feedback in constructive ways helps to build stronger relationships with your colleagues and subordinates.

To deliver effective feedback, follow the following techniques:

1. Be specific: Provide specific feedback about the behavior, action or incident giving an example.

2. Focus on behavior: Focus on behavior that can be changed, followed by a direction for change.

3. Be empathetic: Try to understand the individual's perspective before giving feedback.

4. End with a positive note: Give positive reinforcement and encouragement with feedback to motivate the individual.

Conclusion:

In conclusion, mastering communication skills is vital to success and progress in the workplace. By using the above techniques and strategies, you can increase your communication effectiveness and excel in your profession. The key is to practice and remember that communication is a two-way street; always be aware of what others are saying and what you are saying - this will help strengthen your working relationships and make your workplace experience a positive one.

A study published in the Journal of Applied Physiology found that 7% carbohydrate ingestion increased endurance by 24%, making it clear that fueling your body correctly can have significant performance impacts.

Her regular use of Gatorade has helped her achieve a remarkable 23 Grand Slam wins to date.

Benefits of Choosing Gatorade Products:

Now that the evidence and real-life examples have been presented, let's examine the benefits of choosing Gatorade products:

Hydration:

Gatorade products contain electrolytes that help maintain optimal hydration levels during exercise. Proper hydration improves endurance, cognitive function, and strength.

Nutrition:

Gatorade products contain carbohydrates that help fuel the body for optimal performance during exercise. Carb consumption can increase endurance and offer the body an essential energy source.

Using Gatorade products provides benefits like:

- Improved cognitive function
- Reduced risk of cramping
- Improved recovery

Conclusion:

Every athlete has a different set of needs, which tailor the approach they take towards their nutrition and hydration needs. However, in the world of sports performance, Gatorade has been a go-to solution for athletes for over 50 years. Its reputation can be backed up by an extensive body of research, real-life examples of renowned athletes, and the benefits of using Gatorade products. Using Gatorade can help athletes maintain an optimal balance of hydration and nutrition, leading to improved endurance, cognitive function, recovery, and reduced risk of cramping. These benefits are not to be taken lightly and should be considered when choosing the right athletic performance products. As the world of sports continues to progress, the importance of athletic performance products like Gatorade becomes increasingly clear. Choosing the right products for your unique needs can make all the difference in achieving your athletic goals.

What type of baits are preferred for catching grouper, and what size of baitfish is recommended?
Generate according to: Of all the regions in Florida, mine is the best known for its grouper fishing. The best time to target grouper in my region is during the winter months when the fish come in closer to shore, but we do catch them on a regular basis all year long. We have a lot of different species of grouper, but during the summer the fish are going to be out a lot deeper than in winter, and we’ll catch mostly red and gag grouper, along with the occasional true black grouper.
The water temperatures are considerably warmer in the summer months, so the fish are going to be out a lot deeper where they’re more comfortable. I wouldn’t start looking for them until I hit about 75 feet of water, and from there I’d work westward out to deeper water. A lot of the best fishing is going to be in 100 feet of water or more.
Because grouper are such a structure oriented fish, you’re going to want to look for a stretch of hard bottom (rocks) that has some relief or shelves for the fish to get under. Grouper like to lie in or near the rocks and ambush food as it goes by. The majority of fish that you’re targeting are 10 to 20 pounds, so you want to use heavy tackle so you can pull them away from the rocks and keep them from breaking off your line.
My standard grouper tackle is a 60 to 80 pound conventional outfit with a 7 to 8 foot rod so you have a lot of lifting power to move the fish and once you get their head raised you can lift on the rod and keep them coming away from the structure. More often than not, I fish 80 pound line, usually braided line because it has a thinner diameter so you don’t get at much friction in the water from the current and can thus use less weight to get to the bottom. Also, braided line doesn’t stretch, so when you’re fighting a fish, you don’t lose any ground to line stretch.
To my line, I’ll attach a swivel and about five feet of 80 to 125 pound test leader and a 6/0 to 9/0 4X circle hook depending on the size of the bait. You can catch grouper on dead bait like grunt plugs or half a threadfin, but I prefer live pinfish or pigfish about the size of your hand. Both these baits like to swim on the bottom and are easy for the grouper to catch. You can also use sardines, large pilchards, mullet or just about any 4 to 8 inch baitfish you can find. Depending on the depth and current speed you’ll likely need between 6 and 9 ounces of lead to get the bait to the bottom and keep it there. Place the lead above the swivel on the main line.
If the bottom structure you find is all flat rock, then you can drift and bounce the bottom with your bait and do well on the grouper, but most of the time we’re fishing structure with a lot of relief on it, so I like to anchor up and drop the baits. Grouper don’t respond to the chum like snapper do, so you’re going to have to fish around the structure to get a bite. You’re going to lose some rig and fish in the structure, that’s a given, but you’ll also land a bunch of fish.
The thing to remember is that you only have to land one grouper to get a meal. Land a couple of them, and you can call up your friends and invite them over for dinner. The summertime grouper fishing isn’t as good as the winter, but it’s definitely worth doing because the fish are still out there and they’re hungry, so all you have to do is find them to catch a fresh grouper dinner.
completion: For catching grouper in my region, live pinfish or pigfish are the preferred baits, about the size of your hand. Dead bait like grunt plugs or half a threadfin also work but live bait is the way to go if possible. Other options for baitfish include sardines, large pilchards, mullet, or any 4 to 8 inch baitfish you can find. Depending on the depth and current, 6 to 9 ounces of lead is recommended to get the bait to the bottom and keep it there. The majority of the fish are 10 to 20 pounds, so heavy tackle is necessary. A 60 to 80 pound conventional outfit with a 7 to 8 foot rod and 80-pound braided line is recommended. A 6/0 to 9/0 4X circle hook is appropriate depending on the size of the bait.

2. Consistent Messaging: All messaging across platforms will be uniform and resonate with the brand's core values and mission. 

3. Reactive & Curated Content: Posting or repurposing relevant articles or blog posts, in addition to the overall linking to related topics or industries, would be used.

4. Interactive Content: Interactive content such as quizzes, polls, or contests will be incorporated regularly, this encourages engagement and creates more vitality around the brand.

5. Trending Events: Creating social media content relevant to trending events or significant happenings in the market or community.

Engagement Strategy 

Interacting with the audience will lead to a more engaging and active community. The following tactics will be used for engagement:

1. Prompt Responses: Required to provide timely replies to comments, questions, or direct messages, to show a true interest in customers and gain their trust.

2. Customized Chats: Often, a personal touch goes a long way; therefore, Personalizing replies or conversations could help distinguish the underlying engagement from other ongoing interactions.

3. User-Generated Content: Reposting user-generated content or incorporating people's images or videos with the brand in them, give the opportunity to engage and promote the people who have supported the brand.

4. Collaboration: Collaborating with other brands or industry leaders to increase the reach of the brand.

5. Direct Engagement: Tagging users or influencers in the targeted demographic to increase the chances of brand awareness and interact with possible brand ambassadors.

Growth Strategy 

Growing the community should be a key objective of social media community building. The following tactics will be used for growth:

1. Paid Social Ads: Promoting content with paid social ads to increase the reach and exposure of the brand to the targeted demographic.

2. Collaboration as Guest Content: Collaborating with industry leaders or micro-influencers to post content on their platforms, this will allow the brand to reach a new targeted demographic

3. Consistent Posting: Posting consistently with the suggestions of each platform's algorithm to engage the algorithms and increase social media impressions.

4. Engaging Every Opportunity: Engaging every opportunity to interact with other users or influencers and drive brand exposure

5. Influencer Marketing: Collaborating with other influencer accounts for product placements and promotions to broaden the brand awareness and attract new followers.

Recommended Brands Voice and Tone & Visual Style 

The brand's voice and tone will maintain a consistent, engaging, and authentic tone to resonate with the target demographic. The visual style to be used will also be consistent with the brand's essence and convey the brand's imagery and tone.

Key Performance Indicators 

The Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) chosen to measure social media community building's effectiveness includes reach, impressions, engagement, social media responses, conversions, clicks, and increase in the number of followers. The KPIs would be tracked monthly, and a quarterly / bi-annual report distributed for analysis and adjustment.

Timeline and Budget 

The social media community building strategies outlined in this proposal will be implemented over the period of one year. The total budget for the strategy's execution will be $150,000. A detailed budget breakdown would depend on the objectives of the campaign, the targeted demographic, and the chosen platform. 

Conclusion

Social media community building is a crucial aspect of digital marketing, and with the right strategy, it can enable businesses to better engage with customers and generate loyalty. With this comprehensive proposal, the strategies detailed and the resources proposed will enable the brand to foster a lasting and growing online community. By optimizing content creation, engagement, and growth, the brand can drive site visits, conversions, and increased revenue, setting the tone for future success.

prompt: Create a comprehensive guide detailing step-by-step instructions on how to properly plant and care for various herbs in a garden. Include information on the appropriate soil type, watering and feeding requirements, pest or disease prevention, harvesting methods, and common mistakes to avoid. Use concise language and visual aids such as photographs or diagrams to ensure the guide is easy to navigate and follow.
completion:
Planting and Caring for Herbs in Your Garden: A Comprehensive Guide

Growing your own herbs in your garden allows you to enjoy the fresh, aromatic flavors in your cooking while saving money and reducing waste. However, planting and caring for herbs require some knowledge and skills to ensure their growth and health. In this guide, we will provide you with step-by-step instructions on how to properly plant and care for various herbs in your garden.

Step 1: Choose the Right Location

The first step in growing herbs is to choose the right location for your garden. Most herbs require a minimum of 6 hours of sunlight per day, so choose an area in your garden that receives plenty of sunlight. Herbs also prefer well-draining soils, so avoid planting them in areas that hold water or become boggy after rain.

Step 2: Prepare the Soil

The quality of the soil has a significant impact on the growth and health of your herbs. Before planting, prepare your soil by removing any weeds, rocks, or debris. Then, enrich your soil with compost or organic matter to improve its fertility and structure. You can also add some garden lime to adjust the pH level of your soil to be between 6.0 and 7.0, which is ideal for most herbs.

Step 3: Choose Your Herbs

Herbs come in various types, flavors, and sizes. When selecting herbs for your garden, choose those that are suitable for your climate, soil type, and purpose. Some popular herb choices for gardens include: 

- Basil: best grown in sunny, warm locations in fertile soil 
- Oregano: thrives in well-draining soil and grows best in full sun
- Mint: best grown in partial shade in moist, well-draining soil
- Rosemary: prefers well-draining soil and needs full sun to grow well
- Thyme: grows well in well-draining soil and needs full sun to partial shade

Step 4: Plant Your Herbs

Once you have prepared your soil and decided on your herbs, it's time to plant them. Follow these steps to plant your herbs:

1. Make a hole in the soil that's large enough to accommodate the plant's root ball.
2. Carefully remove the plant from its container and loosen the root ball's edges with your fingers.
3. Place the plant's roots gently into the hole and fill it with soil.
4. Gently press the soil around the plant to secure it.

Step 5: Water Your Herbs

Watering your herbs is crucial to their growth and health. Most herbs prefer to be watered deeply but not too often. Water your herbs once a week or when the soil feels dry to the touch. Be sure to water near the base of the plant instead of overhead to prevent diseases.

Step 6: Feed Your Herbs

To promote the growth and flavor of your herbs, feed them regularly with organic fertilizers. You can use a liquid or granular fertilizer that's low in nitrogen and high in phosphorus, which encourages root growth and flower production. However, be sure not to over-fertilize, as this can lead to problems such as burning or excessive growth.

Step 7: Prevent Pests and Diseases

Herbs are relatively easy to grow, but they are still susceptible to pests and diseases. To prevent these problems, keep your garden clean and free from debris, remove any rotting vegetation, and don't overwater. If you notice any pests or diseases, you can use natural remedies such as insecticidal soap or neem oil to control them.

Step 8: Harvest Your Herbs

Harvesting your herbs at the right time is essential. Most herbs taste best when harvested before they flower or set seed. You can begin harvesting your herbs once they are at least 6 inches tall. Be sure to use sharp scissors or shears to cut the stems cleanly and avoid damaging the plant's leaves.

Step 9: Common Mistakes to Avoid

Some common mistakes to avoid when growing herbs include:

- Overwatering your herbs – Water your herbs only when necessary and avoid watering overhead.
- Using poor-quality soil – Use compost or organic matter to enrich your soil and improve its fertility.
- Not pruning your herbs – Prune your herbs regularly to promote their growth and prevent them from becoming leggy.
- Waiting too long to harvest – Harvest your herbs before they flower or set seed to get the best flavor.

In conclusion, growing herbs in your garden is a rewarding and enjoyable activity. By following these steps, you can plant and care for your herbs properly, prevent pests and diseases, and harvest them at the right time for the freshest and most delicious flavor.

prompt: Write a fictional short story of at least 500 words about two strangers who meet during a challenging time and help each other through it. Include details about the characters' backgrounds, the specific challenges they face, and how they overcome them through teamwork and mutual encouragement. The story should be written in a third-person narration and should have a clear beginning, middle, and an end. Use descriptive language to create a vivid setting and bring the characters to life. The story must illustrate the power of human connection and the importance of empathy and kindness in overcoming difficult circumstances.
completion:
It was a cold November evening in downtown Chicago when Marissa found herself alone and lost. She had just moved to the city to start a new job, and although she had been given a map and directions to her apartment, she had taken a wrong turn and ended up in an unfamiliar neighborhood. It was getting darker, and she was starting to feel uneasy. She clutched her bag tightly and looked around for help.

That's when she saw him. He was sitting on a bench by the side of the road, hunched over and shivering. He looked up and caught her eye, and for a moment, they just stared at each other.

He was an older man, perhaps in his sixties, with a beard and ragged clothes. Marissa could tell that he had been through a lot, and she felt a pang of sympathy for him. She couldn't just leave him there, alone and cold.

"Excuse me," she said softly, approaching him. "Are you alright?"

The man looked up at her, and for a moment, Marissa thought she saw a glimmer of hope in his eyes. "No," he replied, his voice hoarse. "I'm lost. I don't know where to go."

Marissa felt a sense of relief. She knew what it was like to feel lost and alone in a big city. "Here," she said, offering him her hand. "Let me help you."

Together, they set out to find their way. The man was hesitant at first, but Marissa was patient and kind, urging him on at every step. She told him about her own struggles with the city and how she had learned to navigate it over time. She shared some of her favorite places to eat and shop, and they even stopped for a hot cup of coffee at a nearby café to warm up.

As they walked, Marissa learned about the man's life. His name was Tom, and he had lost his job and his home after his wife had passed away. He had been living on the streets for months, trying to survive on his own. She could tell that he was tired and weary, but she also sensed a strength and resilience in him that was admirable.

As they reached the apartment complex, Tom looked up at the building and sighed. "I don't know if I'm ready for this," he said, his voice trembling. "I don't know how to start again."

Marissa put her hand on his shoulder. "You don't have to do it alone, Tom," she said firmly. "We can do it together. I'll help you get settled in, and we'll figure out your next steps."

Together, they walked into the building, and Marissa helped Tom with his bags. She showed him around his new apartment, giving him tips on how to set it up and make it feel like home. She introduced him to her neighbors, and they all welcomed him warmly.

Over the next few days, Marissa and Tom became friends. He joined her for meals, and they would take walks in the park together. They talked about their lives and their dreams, and Marissa shared her plans for the future.

One day, as they were walking in the park, Tom turned to her and said, "I want to thank you, Marissa. You saved my life."

Marissa smiled. "I didn't do anything special," she said. "I just helped someone in need."

Tom shook his head. "No," he said. "You gave me hope. You showed me that there are good people in this world, and that I'm not alone. You gave me a reason to keep going."

Marissa felt a lump in her throat. She had never thought of herself as a hero or a savior. She was just trying to do the right thing, to be kind and compassionate to someone who needed it. But Tom's words touched her deeply, and she knew that she had made a difference in his life.

As the sun set over the city, Marissa and Tom walked back to their apartments. They hugged each other tightly, promising to stay in touch and to be there for each other whenever they needed it. They had faced their challenges together, with empathy and kindness, and they had emerged stronger for it.

And in that moment, Marissa knew that no matter what obstacles she might face in the future, she would always remember the power of human connection and the importance of reaching out to those in need.

prompt: Using research and data, critically examine and evaluate how the proliferation of fake news has influenced the public's perception of public sector employment and unions. Consider the potential consequences on job security, labor relations, and policy outcomes, and assess the effectiveness of current strategies to combat misinformation in these contexts. Provide specific examples to support your analysis and offer recommendations for addressing these challenges moving forward.
completion:
Introduction

The proliferation of fake news has had far-reaching effects, including influencing the public's perception of public sector employment and unions. Unverified information and propaganda have had adverse effects on job security, labor relations, and policy outcomes. The purpose of this essay is to critically examine and evaluate how the proliferation of fake news has impacted the public's perceptions of public sector employment and unions. We will also assess the effectiveness of current strategies to combat misinformation in these contexts, and provide recommendations for addressing these challenges moving forward.


Fake News and Public Perception of Public Sector Employment and Unions

Fake news has influenced the public's perceptions of public sector employment and unions. In recent years, there has been a notable decline in public trust in public sector institutions. This decline can be attributed to the spread of fake news, which has created a climate of skepticism and mistrust.

One example of this is the impact on the public perception of public sector unions. According to a survey by the Pew Research Center, only 33% of Americans have a favorable view of labor unions, with 45% having an unfavorable view (Pew Research Center, 2021). This is a significant shift from previous decades, where labor unions were viewed more favorably. The decline in public trust can be attributed to the spread of fake news that portrays public sector unions as corrupt and self-interested.

Fake news has also impacted the public's perception of public sector employment. Unverified news stories and propaganda have portrayed public sector employees as lazy and overpaid. These false narratives have led to calls for cutting public sector jobs and reducing employee benefits, resulting in job insecurity for public sector employees.

Consequences on Job Security, Labor Relations, and Policy Outcomes

The consequences of fake news on public sector employment and unions are significant. Firstly, it has created job insecurity for public sector employees. Due to the negative perception created by fake news, public sector employees are more likely to face layoffs, reduced benefits, and pay cuts.

Secondly, the spread of fake news has led to strained labor relations. As a result of negative perceptions, public sector unions are less likely to be viewed as legitimate representatives of their members' interests. This has led to a more significant divide between unions and employers, making it more challenging to negotiate labor agreements.

Finally, the impact of fake news has derailed policy outcomes. According to a study by the National Bureau of Economic Research, the decline in public trust in government institutions leads to a decline in government effectiveness (Beland and Cox, 2019). This decline in effectiveness makes it more challenging to address critical public policy issues, such as climate change and social inequality.

Effectiveness of Current Strategies to Combat Misinformation

There are several strategies in place to combat the spread of misinformation. Fact-checking has emerged as a popular way to counter fake news. Social media platforms such as Facebook and Twitter have also implemented measures to combat the spread of fake news, including flagging posts that contain false information.

However, despite these strategies, the spread of fake news continues to undermine the public's perception of public sector employment and unions. Studies have found that fact-checking is only effective when individuals are open to changing their beliefs (Pennycook and Rand, 2019). However, many individuals are not open to changing their beliefs, making it more challenging to combat the spread of fake news.

Recommendations

To address the challenges presented by fake news, several recommendations can be made:

1. Promote Media Literacy: Individuals must be taught to distinguish between real and fake news. This can be achieved by promoting media literacy, teaching individuals to identify credible sources, and critical evaluation of the information they encounter.

2. Enhancing Transparency: The government and public sector organizations must be transparent in their operations. When information is available, it helps to dispel fake news and build public trust. This can be achieved through increased transparency in decision-making processes and the availability of public records.

3. Build Relationships: Public sector organizations must build relationships with the public to counter the negative portrayal in fake news stories. This involves engaging with the public using social media and face-to-face communication.

Conclusion

The proliferation of fake news has had significant implications for the public's perception of public sector employment and unions. It has created job insecurity, strained labor relations, and derailed policy outcomes. The strategies in place to combat the spread of misinformation have not been wholly effective, as many individuals are not open to changing their beliefs. To address these challenges, media literacy can be promoted, transparency can be enhanced, and relationships can be built between public sector organizations and the public. These recommendations will help counter the negative effects of fake news and build trust in public sector institutions.

prompt: Provide a comprehensive guide on how to use Google Ads campaign experiments to enhance website performance. Include step-by-step instructions on setting up experiments, choosing testing parameters, measuring results, and making data-driven decisions for optimization. Additionally, highlight best practices and potential pitfalls to avoid for successful execution of campaign experiments.
completion:
I don't have the practical experience in using google ads campaign experiments. However, I can provide a comprehensive guide by researching and compiling the expert best practices to help you enhance your website performance through google ads campaign experiments.

what are google ads campaign experiments?

google ads campaign experiments feature lets you test and compare changes to your google ads campaigns against your original setup. The tool randomly splits your traffic between your original campaign and the experiment, which you can use to test small and large changes to your campaigns like changing a bidding strategy, ad copy, or even targeting elements.

the tool collects performance data automatically, which you can use to determine whether to make permanent additions or to revert back to the original setup. With enough data, you can make data-driven decisions about your campaigns' elements, which can lead to significant improvements in your campaigns' performance.

how to set up google ads campaign experiments

here’s how:

1. Open your google ads account and click on the campaign you want to test.
2. Click on “drafts and experiments” in the left-hand menu.
3. Click on the “create an experiment” button in the top right corner of the screen.
4. In the “create an experiment” page, you will set the following parameters:
   - experiment type: choose between “split campaign” and “draft and test”.
   - start and end dates: set the duration of the experiment.
   - experiment split (budget): this lets you decide how many of your users will be used in the experiment. The default is 50%, but you can change this amount.
   - name the experiment: add a descriptive name for the experiment.
   - choose the settings you want to test: select one or more settings to test, such as ad copy or bidding strategy.
5. Click on the “save” button.
6. Review the experiment details and start the experiment.

choosing testing parameters

here are some important considerations for choosing testing parameters:

1. Test small changes: start with testing small changes; this would give you the flexibility to switch back to the original setup if you want without making any significant losses.
2. Focus on one element at a time: test one element at a time, such as ad copy or targeting, to help isolate which factor affects your campaigns the most.
3. Keep the experiment short: the longer the experiment, the harder it is to keep everything else unchanged, making it more difficult to compare results accurately.
4. Measure enough data: allow the experiment to run enough to generate meaningful data to help you make informed decisions.

measuring results

here’s how to track and analyze the data from your campaign experiments:

1. Navigate to the “drafts and experiments” page of your google ads account.
2. Click on the experiment you want to analyze.
3. The data will be displayed on the top of the page, highlighting the performance of your original campaign compared to the experiment.
4. Compare the performance of your control and test campaigns based on the metrics you have chosen. Depending on the elements tested, these can include click-through rate, conversion rate, cost per conversion, and many more.
5. Monitor the results over time and make decisions based on meaningful differences.

making data-driven decisions for optimization

once you have enough data, you can make informed decisions about the changes you have made during the experiment:

1. If the experiment's results are better than the original, implement the change as a permanent part of the campaign.
2. If there is no difference or a small difference, it may not be worth implementing the change.
3. If the experiment's results are worse, revert to the original campaign settings.

best practices and potential pitfalls to avoid

finally, here are some best practices and potential pitfalls to avoid when using google ads campaign experiments:

1. Plan your experiments carefully before starting them.
2. Keep your experiment sweet and short.
3. Avoid making too many changes at once, as this can skew your data.
4. Keep your testing objective-focused and have control over only one variable at a time.
5. Monitor the data periodically and analyze it with appropriate statistical methods to make informed decisions.
6. Don't stop a campaign too early or too late during the testing period, measure enough data to make informed decisions.
7. Don't use the tool arbitrarily, only to make untested changes to your campaigns.
8. Avoid significant experiments and changes during peak seasons, but use it during peak traffic periods to get better results.

in conclusion

google ads campaign experiments is a powerful tool to enhance your website performance by testing various elements to see how they impact your campaigns' performance. It's a valuable tool to help you make informed decisions about your campaigns that can significantly impact your business's bottom line. Follow these best practices while avoiding pitfalls to achieve the best outcomes.

Include a breakdown of the syntax and functionality of each language in relation to their respective ecosystems, as well as an evaluation of their respective strengths and weaknesses in terms of performance, scalability, security, and ease of use. Additionally, consider factors such as community support, tooling, and best practices when examining the two languages' suitability for web development projects.
completion:
C# and PHP are both popular programming languages used in back-end web development. While they share certain features, they also differ in terms of syntax and functionality. In this article, we will compare the two languages based on various factors such as performance, scalability, security, ease of use, community support, tooling, and best practices.

Syntax and Functionality

C# is an object-oriented programming language that was developed by Microsoft. It is heavily influenced by C++ and Java, and features strong typing and support for several programming paradigms, including imperative, functional, and declarative programming. C# uses a curly braces syntax and a similar keyword structure to C++, making it relatively easy for developers with experience in those languages to learn.

PHP, on the other hand, is a server-side scripting language designed specifically for web development. It is loosely-typed and supports procedural, object-oriented and functional programming paradigms. PHP uses a mix of curly braces syntax and traditional control structures, such as if/else and while loops, making it relatively easy to learn.

Performance

C# is known for its speed and efficiency. It is a compiled language, which means it can be optimized for performance, resulting in fast-running code. Additionally, C# offers asynchronous programming features, allowing developers to perform non-blocking I/O operations, which can further improve the performance of web applications.

PHP, on the other hand, is an interpreted language, which means it is slower than compiled languages like C#. However, PHP has improved significantly over the years, and with the release of PHP 7, the language's performance has been greatly enhanced, making it much faster than older versions of the language.

Scalability

C# is a scalable language that can handle large-scale projects. It offers various features, such as task parallelism, which allow developers to scale their applications to meet increased demand. Additionally, C# includes .NET framework, which offers a comprehensive set of tools and libraries for building scalable web applications.

PHP is also scalable, but it has some limitations. It works best when used for small to medium-sized applications. However, with the help of various frameworks, such as Laravel and Symfony, developers can build large and complex applications, making it a suitable option for a wide range of web development projects.

Security

C# is a secure language that boasts several inbuilt security features such as type-safe, memory-safe, and strong-typing. Additionally, it supports sandboxing to prevent unauthorized code from running on the server, which is a significant advantage when it comes to security.

PHP, on the other hand, has been criticized for being less secure than other programming languages, in part due to its history of vulnerabilities. However, with the release of PHP 7, significant progress has been made in terms of security.

Ease of Use

C# is a relatively easy language to learn, especially for developers with experience in C++ or Java. It has a well-organized syntax, a range of libraries and tools, and a supportive community, making it easy for developers to create applications.

PHP is also relatively easy to learn, owing to its simple yet consistent syntax. Additionally, PHP has a large and active developer community, which provides a vast pool of resources and a supportive environment for beginners.

Community Support, Tooling, and Best Practices

C# and PHP both have active and dedicated developer communities that provide a wealth of resources and tools, making it easier for developers to build web applications. Additionally, both languages have a range of frameworks and libraries that streamline web development, enabling development teams to rapidly build applications while adhering to best practices.

When it comes to tooling, both languages are well served by an array of third-party tools and development environments. However, the .NET ecosystem offers a more comprehensive set of tools and features for developers, including powerful integrated development environments like Visual Studio.

In terms of best practices, both languages offer a range of techniques and frameworks to promote code organization, maintainability, and scalability. However, C# has a slight advantage here, as it boasts various built-in features, such as interfaces and generics, to help developers write clear, maintainable code.

Conclusion

Overall, C# and PHP are both excellent options for back-end web development. While C# offers better performance, scalability, and security features, PHP has an active development community, simple syntax, and a range of frameworks and libraries that make it a versatile and widely used platform for web development. Ultimately, the ideal language for any given project will depend on the specific needs and constraints of the project and the development team's skills and preferences.

prompt: Write a fictional short story of at least 500 words about a person who decides to learn how to ice skate for the first time as an adult, relating the challenges they face, what they learn about themselves as a result of the experience, and the people they meet or interact with along the way, all while using descriptive language and vivid imagery to engage the reader emotionally.
completion:
As a child, Abby had always been drawn to the icy twirls and jumps of figure skaters on television, but growing up in a small Texas town, ice skating wasn't exactly a commonplace activity. By the time she reached her mid-twenties, Abby had given up on the idea of ever learning how to skate, accepting it as one of those childhood dreams that just never came to fruition.

But one cold December day, as Abby walked past a rink in downtown Dallas, she couldn't help but be drawn in by the glittering lights and the sound of blades slicing through the ice. Before she knew it, she'd impulsively bought a pair of rental skates and was lacing them up, surrounded by children who were half her size and twice as fearless.

For the first few minutes, Abby clung to the wall, barely shuffling her feet forward as she tried to find her balance. Every time someone came even remotely close to her, she flinched and flailed her arms wildly in an attempt to avoid a collision. But slowly, progressively, she gained a little bit of confidence. She let go of the wall, moving tentatively at first but gradually finding her rhythm.

As she skated, Abby began to delight in the sensation of the cold air washing over her face, in the gentle swishing sound of her blades against the ice, in the feeling of her body working in a way it never had before. Every time she managed to complete a full circle around the rink without falling, she let out a sound somewhere between a gasp and a laugh.

But her delight was constantly tempered by frustration and embarrassment. She'd barely been skating for an hour before she accidentally knocked over a little boy, sending him sprawling across the ice. She tried to help him up, but he was crying so hard that his mom came over and gave Abby a long, withering look.

As the day went on, Abby began to notice how effortlessly everyone else seemed to glide around the rink. Children who could barely toddle seemed to be able to move around with far more grace and skill than she could muster. One man in particular stood out to her - he was obviously an experienced skater, spinning and weaving around the other people on the rink with complete confidence. Abby couldn't help but watch him, feeling a deep pang of envy.

But then the man caught her eye and flashed her a friendly smile. "Keep at it," he said, as he wove past her. "It looks like you're really getting the hang of it."

Abby tried to smile back, but she was already off balance and stumbling. "Thanks," she said, as she flailed her arms for balance.

As she left the rink at the end of the day, Abby felt a curious mix of emotions. She was exhausted, with blisters already forming on her feet from the rental skates. But she was also elated, feeling a sense of accomplishment for trying something new and sticking with it, even though it was hard.

Over the next few weeks, Abby found herself drawn back to the ice rink again and again. She still fell down frequently and regularly had to dodge swarms of hyperactive children, but she was starting to figure out how to control her movements and develop a sense of balance. She even started to take private lessons, working on her posture and technique with a strict but kind instructor who refused to let her give up.

The more time Abby spent on the ice, the more she realized that it wasn't just a matter of learning how to skate. She was learning something about herself - about her persistence and resilience, about her ability to push past discomfort and fear in order to achieve something that mattered to her.

But perhaps most surprisingly, Abby was finding that she was beginning to form connections with the people around her. She no longer dreaded the inevitable crashes or collisions, as she knew that other skaters would be there to help her up and offer a kind word of encouragement. There was a sense of camaraderie on the ice, a shared sense of joy and challenge.

One chilly January evening, Abby found herself skating alongside the man who had encouraged her on her first day at the rink. They chatted as they skated, exchanging stories about their lives and joking about the absurdity of trying to balance their bodies on blades of steel. As they parted ways at the end of the night, Abby felt a sense of warmth in her chest - the knowledge that she was capable of learning a new skill, of forming new connections, and of finding joy in something entirely unexpected.

prompt: Write a comprehensive and detailed list of ten specific techniques or strategies that can be implemented to improve one's leadership proficiency. These strategies should encompass methods like empowering others, setting measurable goals, and creating an environment of trust and innovation. Additionally, the list should utilize concrete examples and thoroughly discuss the benefits of each technique in terms of its real-world applications.
completion:
1. Active Listening: A leader must have excellent listening skills to understand the concerns of stakeholders better. Active listening involves giving undivided attention to people and not interrupting them while they are speaking.

For example, a team leader may have a weekly meeting with their team to discuss any issues and listen to their suggestions on how to improve work processes. By actively listening to the team members, the leader can gain insights into the problems and come up with practical solutions.

Benefits: Active listening can improve a leader's relationship with their team, build trust and create a more collaborative working environment.

2. Empowering Others: A leader's responsibility is not to micromanage or control every aspect of their team's work. Instead, they should empower their team members by delegating tasks and giving them autonomy.

For example, a manager can give a team member an important project with clear objectives and guidelines. This allows the employee to take ownership of the project and make decisions based on their expertise.

Benefits: Empowering others can improve employee morale, increase productivity, and enhance problem-solving skills.

3. Setting Measurable Goals: A leader should set specific, measurable goals for their team to achieve. This helps to keep the team focused and motivated towards a common objective.

For example, a project manager can set a goal to complete a project within a certain timeline and budget. This helps the team to stay on track and identify potential issues before they become significant challenges.

Benefits: Setting measurable goals can improve team performance, increase accountability and provide a clear direction towards success.

4. Encouraging Creativity: A leader should encourage innovation and creativity in their team. This can lead to new ideas and solutions to problems that have not been considered before.

For example, a CEO can encourage employees to participate in brainstorming sessions that generate new ideas for products, services or processes. This can lead to more efficient work processes, new products or services, and improved customer experiences.

Benefits: Encouraging creativity can enhance innovation, increase employee engagement, and create more effective solutions.

5. Building Trust: Trust is a key element in any successful relationship, whether in personal or professional realms. A leader must build trust with their team members to create a positive working environment.

For example, a team leader may consistently demonstrate their competence in managing the team, ensure that they keep their promises, and be transparent in their communication. This builds trust between the leader and the team members.

Benefits: Building trust can improve employee motivation, enhance performance, and create a positive work environment.

6. Promoting Collaboration: Collaboration involves working together towards a common goal. A leader should encourage collaboration within their team to harness the strengths of individual members to achieve a common objective.

For example, a sales manager can bring together sales and marketing teams to work on an integrated marketing campaign for a new product launch. This promotes collaboration between both teams and generates better results.

Benefits: Promoting collaboration fosters innovation, increases productivity, and creates a sense of community among team members.

7. Practicing Emotional Intelligence: Emotional intelligence involves understanding and managing one's emotions and the emotions of others. A leader must practice emotional intelligence to maintain a positive team culture and effective communication.

For example, a CEO can recognize the emotional state of employees and provide emotional support when they face significant life events or work problems. This creates a safe and supportive environment that promotes employee well-being and productivity.

Benefits: Practicing emotional intelligence can improve morale, create a positive work environment, and enhance communication skills.

8. Establishing Accountability: A leader must establish accountability within their team to ensure that everyone is responsible for their actions and work output.

For example, a project manager can require each team member to submit regular reports detailing their progress and identifying any issues. This creates accountability and ensures that problems are addressed promptly.

Benefits: Establishing accountability improves performance, increases self-awareness, and fosters a sense of responsibility among team members.

9. Promoting Continuous Learning: A leader should encourage continuous learning within their team members to stay up to date with industry trends and advancements.

For example, a senior manager can facilitate training sessions and workshops for their employees to improve their technical skills, soft skills, or knowledge of new technologies.

Benefits: Promoting continuous learning enhances employee performance, increases employee retention, and boosts team productivity.

10. Balancing Work with Life: A leader should ensure that their team members have a healthy work-life balance to prevent burnout and maintain employee well-being.

For example, a manager can offer flexible working hours, paid time off, or other benefits that support a healthy work-life balance. This creates a positive work environment and promotes employee satisfaction and loyalty.

Benefits: Balancing work with life enhances employee well-being, reduces employee absenteeism, and improves retention rates.

prompt: Create a mystery novel about a detective who solves a case involving a kidnapping.
completion:
Chapter One 

Detective John Smith sat at his desk, twirling his pen in his hand as he stared at the stack of papers in front of him. The case had been open for weeks, but he still didn't have any leads. A young girl, Sarah Thompson, had disappeared from her home in the middle of the night. Her parents had woken up to an empty bed and an open window. There were no signs of a struggle, no witnesses, and no ransom demands. It was as if she had vanished into thin air. 

John rubbed his eyes, trying to shake off the fatigue that had settled in his bones. He had been working on this case nonstop since it was assigned to him, and he was running out of ideas. He needed a break, a fresh perspective, something that would help him crack the case. 

Just then, his phone rang. He answered it, half expecting it to be his boss with an update on the case. Instead, he heard a woman's voice on the other end. 

"Hello, Detective Smith? My name is Katherine, and I need your help. My son has been kidnapped." 

Chapter Two 

John arrived at Katherine's house to find her pacing back and forth in the living room. She was a well-dressed woman in her early forties, her blonde hair pulled back in a tight ponytail. When she saw him, she rushed over and grabbed his hand. 

"Thank you for coming, Detective. I don't know what to do. They took my son, Jack, in the middle of the night. They left a note, demanding a ransom of one million dollars. I don't have that kind of money." 

John sat down, pulling his notebook from his pocket. "Tell me everything you remember, from the moment you realized Jack was missing." 

Katherine took a deep breath, then began. "I woke up in the middle of the night to the sound of footsteps in the hallway. I thought it was Jack, coming back from the bathroom. But when I opened my eyes, I saw a shadowy figure in the doorway. I screamed, but before I could do anything else, they grabbed Jack and disappeared out the window. That's when I found the note." 

John nodded, making notes as he listened. "Did you recognize the intruder? Could you tell if it was a man or a woman?" 

Katherine shook her head. "It was too dark to see anything. All I could make out was their silhouette." 

John stood up, putting his notebook away. "Don't worry, Mrs. Johnson. We'll do everything we can to find your son. I'll need a list of everyone who has access to your house, as well as any enemies or suspicious acquaintances you or your son may have." 

Chapter Three 

John spent the rest of the day going over the details of the case with his partner, Eva. They combed through the list of suspects, trying to put together the pieces of the puzzle. But as the hours ticked by, they still had no leads. 

Just when John was about to call it a night, his phone rang. It was Katherine again. 

"Detective, I just received another note. They lowered the ransom to five hundred thousand dollars. What do I do?" 

John's heart sank. He knew that a kidnapper who didn't receive their ransom was likely to become violent. He had to act fast. 

"Stay calm, Mrs. Johnson. I'm on my way. We'll have to set up a drop-off location and coordinate with the kidnapper. We'll need a team to monitor the area, and I'll need you to make the exchange." 

Katherine's voice trembled. "Okay, Detective. I'll do whatever it takes to get my son back." 

Chapter Four 

The drop-off point was a deserted alleyway on the outskirts of town. John and Eva parked down the street, watching as Katherine walked toward where they had set up the money. They couldn't see the kidnapper, but they knew he was watching from somewhere nearby. 

As Katherine put the bag of money down, a shadowy figure emerged from the darkness. John's heart raced as he recognized the same silhouette Katherine had described in her initial report. The kidnapper snatched up the bag and disappeared into the night. 

John and Eva waited a few agonizing minutes before moving in. They found the kidnapper trying to escape through a back alley, holding a bag of money in one hand and a knife in the other. John tackled him to the ground, disarming him with a quick swipe. 

Back at the station, they made the arrest and searched the kidnapper's hideout. There they found Jack, a little shaken but unharmed. 

As John watched the family tearfully reunite, he couldn't help but feel a sense of accomplishment. Another case solved, another criminal behind bars. But most importantly, another life saved.

The fairies stood their ground; there was no turning back now. Terra put out her hands and began to chant, creating a powerful earthquake that shook the room.

Zephyr's gust collided with Terra's massive tremors, causing an enormous whirlwind to form. Blaze summoned a tremendous inferno, which incinerated anything that crossed its path.

Despite Malakar's best efforts, he was no match for the fairies' combined strength. The crystal was reclaimed, and the balance of the world was restored.

With the crystal returned to its rightful place, the forest began to flourish once more, and the world was filled with happiness and light.

The fairies were hailed as heroes, their names etched in the history of the kingdom. From that day forth, they remained the guardians of the forest, and the balance was never again upset.

The fairies had learned many lessons on their journey, but the most significant of all was the power of friendship and the need for loyalty and courage in a time of crisis. They knew that together they could overcome any obstacle, and that they were stronger for it.

Question/Instruction: Can you summarize the history of the Burnet House and its significance in ending the Civil War?

Given material: City Club Apartments at Third and Vine is in a remodeled 1928 building on the most historic corner in Cincinnati.
The most historic corner in the city will soon be bustling once again. The northwest corner of Third and Vine streets was the site of the Burnet House, the famous 19th-century hotel that played an important role in ending the Civil War.
City Club Apartments is renovating the former PNC Annex building at 309 Vine St. Into luxury apartments, along with a marketplace, café and rooftop restaurant. The first tenants are moving in this month.
The renovation includes restoring many of the original features in the lobby of the beaux-arts-style annex built for Union Central Life Insurance Co. In 1928, including the marble walls, decorative metal work, ornate ceilings and white-on-black maps of old Cincinnati along the frieze.
In the foyer, an aged bronze tablet original to the building features a bas-relief bust of prominent early settler Jacob Burnet and tells the site’s storied history.
“This site was occupied before 1802 by an Indian mound”: Early settlers found elliptical Indian burial mounds built by the ancient Adena people throughout the Cincinnati basin.
In his 1815 book “Natural and Statistical View, or Picture of Cincinnati,” Dr. Daniel Drake described a large mound east of Race Street at Fifth Street that extended nearly to this site.
“From 1802-1825 by the estate of Judge Jacob Burnet”: Burnet was a judge and politician in the Northwest Territory, a U.S. Senator and president of Cincinnati College. Debts forced him to sell his mansion in 1825, and he moved to Seventh and Elm streets.
In 1842, William Shires used the property for a summer garden and theater with a restaurant in the Burnet mansion. Shires’ Garden burned down in 1848.
“From 1850-1926 by the Burnet House”: Designed by renowned architect Isaiah Rogers, “the finest hotel in the world,” as claimed by the Illustrated London News, boasted 340 rooms and modern amenities like running water.
The H-shaped hotel was capped with a dome in the middle, making it look more like a capitol building. A grand tiered staircase led to Ionic columns at the entrance.
Every notable Queen City visitor, from Oscar Wilde to Jenny Lind, future presidents to a future king (Edward VII), stayed at the Burnet House. Abraham Lincoln was a guest twice, the last time on his birthday en route to his inauguration.
On March 20, 1864, Gens. Ulysses S. Grant and William Tecumseh Sherman met in Parlor A on the second floor, spread out maps and made the plans for how to end the Civil War. The beginning of the end happened there.
Architect James W. McLaughlin supervised a major remodel in 1885. The dome was removed, and a new main entrance was created on Vine Street.
By the 1920s, the city’s activities had shifted away from the river to the financial and shopping districts on Fourth and Fifth streets. Mid-19th-century modern was outdated, and the Burnet House was torn down in 1926.
Union Central Life Insurance purchased the site to build an annex to their distinctive neoclassical skyscraper at Fourth and Vine streets. The plan was an 18-story structure in the same style, but only the first nine-story section was completed. The buildings have been occupied by Central Trust Bank and PNC Bank.
The annex building has a similar H-shape and configuration as the remodeled Burnet House in possible homage. The spirit of the Burnet House lingers at the site.

Located on the most historic corner of Cincinnati, the hotel was designed by renowned architect Isaiah Rogers and boasted 340 rooms and modern amenities like running water. Every notable Queen City visitor, including Abraham Lincoln twice, stayed at the Burnet House. On March 20, 1864, Gens. Ulysses S. Grant and William Tecumseh Sherman met in Parlor A on the second floor, spread out maps and made the plans for how to end the Civil War. The beginning of the end happened there. The Burnet House was torn down in 1926, but the remodeled PNC Annex building at 309 Vine St. Has a similar H-shape and configuration as a possible homage to the Burnet House. prompt: Write a first-person point of view short story, consisting of at least 500 words, about a person who discovers they have the power to travel between parallel universes. Incorporate at least two distinct, fully-realized parallel universes in your story, describing the differences between them in detail. Include a dilemma or conflict faced by the protagonist that can only be resolved by traveling to a different universe, and ensure that the resolution of this conflict has significant consequences for both universes involved. Use vivid language, sensory details, and creative imagery to make the worlds come to life for the reader.
completion:
I was always fascinated by the concept of parallel universes. It seemed almost too good to be true that there could be multiple versions of myself living in different worlds, experiencing different realities. But never in my wildest dreams could I have imagined that I would one day be able to travel between them.

It all started on an ordinary morning. I was getting ready for work, sipping my coffee and scrolling through my social media feed when I felt a sudden dizzying sensation. The world around me seemed to warp and contort before my very eyes, and before I knew it, I was standing in a completely different place.

It took me a few moments to register what was happening. It was like nothing I had ever experienced before. I was standing in a bustling city, surrounded by towering skyscrapers, but everything was just slightly off. The colors were brighter, the air smelled sweeter, and the people moving around me were dressed in clothes from another era.

It finally dawned on me that I had somehow stumbled into a parallel universe. I was equal parts ecstatic and terrified by the realization. On the one hand, I now had the power to explore alternate realities, and on the other hand, I had no idea how to control it. 

The first few times, the jumps were sudden and involuntary, but over time I learned to harness the power within me. And so my adventures began.

I traveled to worlds where the sky was always purple, where technology was thousands of years ahead of ours, and to a world where the dinosaurs never went extinct. But the two universes that left the biggest impression on me were the ones that were almost identical to our own world.

In one universe, I discovered a world where the economic divide was nonexistent. Everyone was equal and lived in harmony. The social support systems were impeccable, and people seemed to be generally happier. Everything just worked here, from the education system to the political infrastructure.

In the other, however, the opposite was true. The world was a dystopian nightmare, where the rich ruled with an iron fist and the poor were left to scavenge for scraps. There was a cloud of despair hanging over the entire world, and the people seemed to have given up hope of ever seeing a brighter future.

I knew that I had to make a choice. I could continue traveling through the universes, living out my wildest fantasies or try to make a difference. My decision was easy — I had to intervene.

I started by trying to help the people in the dystopian universe. I gathered resources from different universes, working hard to support the people living in poverty. For a while, things seemed to be improving. Crime rates had dropped, and the overall morale of the people had increased. It seemed as though the dystopian world was actually on the path to recovery.

But the problem was that I couldn't stay there forever. I had people who loved me in my original universe, responsibilities that needed attending to. And when I returned home after being away for so long, I found that things had changed. My mother had fallen ill, and the world around me was slipping into chaos. 

There was no other solution. I had to leave my universe and travel to the alternate one where everything worked seamlessly. I knew it was the only way to save my mother, and I couldn't bear the thought of losing her. 

It took me several days to prepare, and when I finally made the jump, the difference was immediate. The hospital she was in was well-staffed, and the treatment was prompt and efficient. She recovered quickly, and I knew that this world had saved her.

But now, I had created a new problem. By taking valuable resources from one universe to fix another, I had upset the balance. The world that worked so well initially was now starting to collapse, and I knew it was all my fault. I had to find a way to fix it, to make things right.

It hasn't been easy, but I'm trying. I'm gathering a team of people from all the worlds I have visited, trying to create a balance between the different realities. It's a lot of responsibility, but I know I can make it work.

Who knows what my next adventure will lead to, but one thing is certain, I now have a mission. I want to explore the endless possibilities that come with traveling through the parallel universes while also making sure that each one is a world worth living in.

Mining Poems or Odes, produced as part of last year's Bridging the Gap: Resilience programme, is currently a Top Staff Pick on Vimeo and it's great to see it's getting a warm reaction in the comments feed!
When Lisa Clarkson saw "Mining Poems or Odes" for the first time, it inspired her to write this response. Lisa is a graduate from Screen Academy Scotland. She says she wants to be a writer when she grows up, or a Foley Artist. Lisa lives and works in Edinburgh.
How can it be that an arrangement of words and pictures can start what feels like a fire inside your belly? I saw a short film directed by Callum Rice one Friday morning and it did this - it sang to me. Despite the star of the film being a roll-up smoking auld gadge, the beauty of Mining Poems or Odes is undeniably true and somehow pure. A primarily talking head style video of Robert, a former shipyard welder, intercut with scenes of shipyard life and Glasgow tenements shouldn't be this exciting. But the way in which it sings is just gorgeous. A lyrical love story to Glasgow and its lost industry. Robert’s deep sense of pride as both welder and poet is infectious. The way in which he entwines the two crafts is beautiful; and the way in which he is presented is too.
watching this film is dangerous. It says go forth Workers… women… unschooled poets! And WRITE.
As expected of a film about poetry, the musicality of the piece was stunning. Smoky velvety strings haunt Robert’s soft words, rising and falling with the speaker, at odds with the craggy face. Further more it is visually arresting, with Rice choosing soft and dreamy images of ultra masculine settings, thus showing the themes of which Robert speaks - of the whole man. This whole man - a man of words and body. Men of great physical strength, huge men throwing weights ‘about for fun’ - the same men who show real emotion and sincerity in an ‘alright son?’. Men who speak and think with an intimidating strength.
Robert’s ‘trade in blood and human bone’ sticks to the memory just as vividly as Edwin Morgan’s shilpit dogs or roses of mould. Images too cling to memory: Robert’s crumpled face and the Glasgow red-stone gargoyles - the battered Wordsworth copy of The Ragged Trousered Philanthropist which sits beside Robert’s ashtray and notebooks, all of life’s essentials - the welder’s helmet and the sparks exploding in front of it - Callum Rice’s visual poetry is as equally delicate and brash as Robert’s spoken words are.
Of all Robert’s words there is one which clings to mind the most - MINING - ‘what a word’ he says - indeed. As a junior writer (in a senior body) ‘mining’ wraps up the slog, the mental gymnastics of working to find a gem - the perfect word, to place within words, within sentences and structures, within characters, inside worlds. Mining - groping about blindly; in the dark, frightening, probably ugly and yet completely intangible depths of your own mind for the right thing to say. So easy to give up and listen to multitude of other voices and get on with real life, to shut up. The hardest work is to keep mining.
